source.label: 原创进阶练习
source.notice: 本文与题目为原创教学材料，不是考试真题。人物、机构与项目为虚构练习情境；难度等级仅供学习安排参考。

listening.title: 图书馆的新安排
listening.subtitle: A Different Kind of Library Seat
listening.body:
Last term, our college library received complaints about group discussions near the silent study area. At first, the staff considered banning all conversation on that floor. However, a student survey showed that many people needed a place to work together between classes. So the library tried a different arrangement.

It moved several tables into an unused room near the entrance. Students can book these tables for forty-five minutes, and there is a whiteboard beside each one. The silent area remains upstairs. During the first week, some students found the booking system confusing. In response, the staff put simple instructions on every table and shortened the online form.

The new arrangement is flexible because it supports different kinds of study. It also shows why listening to users matters. A complete ban would have solved one problem by creating another. Now, both individual learners and project groups have somewhere suitable to go.

vocabulary.meaning: 灵活的；能适应不同需要的

questions.prompt: What is the talk mainly about?
options: How a library found space for different study needs.
Why students should stop studying in groups.
How the college built a larger library.
Why online booking should be removed completely.
questions.explanation: 全文先提出安静学习与小组讨论的冲突，再介绍分区安排，重点是兼顾不同学习需求。
questions.quote: The new arrangement is flexible because it supports different kinds of study.

questions.prompt: How long can students book a group table for?
options: Twenty minutes.
Thirty minutes.
Forty-five minutes.
One hour.
questions.explanation: 原文明确说明每次可以预约 forty-five minutes，即 45 分钟。
questions.quote: Students can book these tables for forty-five minutes, and there is a whiteboard beside each one.

questions.prompt: What can we infer about the library staff?
options: They preferred to ignore problems with the booking system.
They were willing to improve the plan after receiving feedback.
They believed silent study was no longer necessary.
They planned to reserve the new room only for teachers.
questions.explanation: 发现预约系统令人困惑后，工作人员增加说明并简化表格，说明他们愿意根据反馈调整方案。
questions.quote: In response, the staff put simple instructions on every table and shortened the online form.

questions.prompt: What does "flexible" mean in this talk?
options: Expensive to maintain.
Available only at night.
Difficult to understand.
Able to meet different needs.
questions.explanation: 后面的 because 引出解释：它支持不同学习方式，因此 flexible 在此意为能适应不同需求的。
questions.quote: The new arrangement is flexible because it supports different kinds of study.

listening.title: 修理角的第一天
listening.subtitle: Learning at the Repair Corner
listening.body:
On Saturday, I took a broken desk lamp to a repair event at our community centre. I expected a volunteer to fix it while I waited. Instead, a retired engineer invited me to sit beside her and describe what had happened to it. We checked the cable together and discovered a loose connection.

Before the event, I had thought repair required expensive equipment and years of training. This small experience challenged that assumption. The engineer explained each step, but she also made clear that some electrical jobs should be left to trained people. The aim was not to make visitors attempt every repair themselves.

By the end of the afternoon, I had a working lamp and a better understanding of it. The organisers hope the event will restore people's interest in caring for everyday objects. They plan to hold it monthly, with separate tables for clothing, furniture, and simple household items.

questions.prompt: What does the speaker mainly describe?
options: A plan to sell repaired lamps online.
A course for becoming a professional engineer.
An event that helped the speaker understand and care for an object.
A complaint about the cost of household equipment.
questions.explanation: 叙述重点既包括修好台灯，也包括在共同检查中学到知识，因而是一次增进理解的修理体验。
questions.quote: By the end of the afternoon, I had a working lamp and a better understanding of it.

questions.prompt: What problem did they find in the lamp?
options: A loose connection.
A missing switch.
A damaged shade.
A broken wooden base.
questions.explanation: 二人共同检查电线后发现的是 loose connection，即连接松动。
questions.quote: We checked the cable together and discovered a loose connection.

questions.prompt: Which lesson does the engineer seem to support?
options: Visitors should repair every electrical item alone.
Only brand-new objects are worth understanding.
A successful repair requires expensive tools in every case.
Learning about repairs also includes recognising one's limits.
questions.explanation: 工程师一边解释步骤，一边强调部分电气工作需要交给专业人士，因此学习还包括认识能力边界。
questions.quote: The engineer explained each step, but she also made clear that some electrical jobs should be left to trained people.

questions.prompt: In this talk, "restore people's interest" means to do what?
options: Measure how much money people spend.
Bring back people's interest.
Replace people's belongings.
Record people's addresses.
questions.explanation: restore 表示使某种状态重新出现；在这里是重新唤起人们爱护日常物品的兴趣。
questions.quote: The organisers hope the event will restore people's interest in caring for everyday objects.

listening.title: 一份更清楚的交接
listening.subtitle: A Better Handover
listening.body:
When I joined a small design company, I noticed that our Monday meetings often lasted more than an hour. Everyone described what they had done, but we still left without knowing who needed help. My manager asked me to suggest a more useful format.

I proposed a brief written update before the meeting. Each person would list a completed task, a current difficulty, and one decision they needed from the team. The meeting itself would focus on the difficulties and decisions, rather than repeat the entire update.

We tested the format for three weeks. The meetings became shorter, although writing the updates took some preparation. One colleague worried that quiet members might still be overlooked. We therefore added a short round in which everyone could raise an issue. The manager said the goal was not simply to save minutes. It was to make sure the time we spent together led to action.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of the new meeting format?
options: To let the manager speak for longer.
To turn shared meeting time into useful action.
To remove all written communication.
To compare employees' working hours.
questions.explanation: 结尾明确指出目标不只是省时间，而是让共同讨论带来行动。
questions.quote: It was to make sure the time we spent together led to action.

questions.prompt: What should each written update include?
options: A personal story, a salary request, and a customer review.
A full project history and a list of every email.
Only the number of tasks completed during the week.
A completed task, a difficulty, and a decision needed.
questions.explanation: 原文列出了三个项目：已完成任务、当前困难，以及需要团队作出的一个决定。
questions.quote: Each person would list a completed task, a current difficulty, and one decision they needed from the team.

questions.prompt: Why was a short speaking round added?
options: To make room for people who might not speak up otherwise.
To make every meeting last at least an hour.
To allow colleagues to repeat all their written updates.
To prevent employees from asking questions.
questions.explanation: 新增轮流发言环节是为了回应安静成员可能被忽略的担忧，让他们也有明确的表达机会。
questions.quote: One colleague worried that quiet members might still be overlooked.

questions.prompt: What does "brief" mean in "a brief written update"?
options: Highly private.
Unusually expensive.
Short and concise.
Written by a lawyer.
questions.explanation: brief 在此修饰工作进展说明，表示简短的，不是其他语境中的法律文件之意。
questions.quote: I proposed a brief written update before the meeting.

listening.title: 不只是一张校园地图
listening.subtitle: Testing the Campus Map
listening.body:
Our student technology club developed a map to help new students find their way around campus. The first version showed the shortest walking route between buildings. We thought this would be enough, but a group of testers quickly pointed out several problems. Some routes included locked gates, while others had steep steps.

We realised that a useful map had to be reliable, not merely attractive. The club visited each route and added notes about opening hours, steps, and covered paths. We also placed a feedback button on the page so users could report changes.

At the launch event, people paid more attention to these practical details than to the map's colours. One tester explained that the best route depended on the person and the weather. The project taught us to question an easy assumption: the shortest route is not always the most suitable one. Regular checks will now be part of our work.

questions.prompt: What did the club learn from developing the map?
options: The colours of a map matter more than its information.
Users always prefer the shortest possible route.
Feedback should be collected only after a project ends.
A useful tool needs accurate details and an understanding of users.
questions.explanation: 测试使团队发现最短路线不一定适合使用者，之后补充实地核查和实用信息，体现了准确性和使用需求的重要性。
questions.quote: We realised that a useful map had to be reliable, not merely attractive.

questions.prompt: Which problem did the testers discover?
options: The map could be opened only in the library.
Some suggested routes passed through locked gates.
The buildings had recently changed their names.
There were no colours on the first version.
questions.explanation: 测试者发现部分路线涉及锁着的门，还有些包含陡峭台阶。
questions.quote: Some routes included locked gates, while others had steep steps.

questions.prompt: Why will regular checks be necessary?
options: The club wants to change the colours every week.
Every student follows exactly the same route.
Information about routes may change after the map is launched.
The campus will no longer have any gates.
questions.explanation: 页面允许使用者报告变化，团队也会定期检查，可推知路线信息需要持续维护。
questions.quote: We also placed a feedback button on the page so users could report changes.

questions.prompt: What does "reliable" mean in this talk?
options: Able to be trusted.
Easy to decorate.
Difficult to download.
Available for a high price.
questions.explanation: 这里强调路线是否真实可用，因此 reliable 表示信息可信、可以依赖。
questions.quote: We realised that a useful map had to be reliable, not merely attractive.

listening.title: 赶车还是换条路
listening.subtitle: An Alternative Way to Travel
listening.body:
For several months, I took the same bus to my evening language class. It stopped close to my flat, but it often arrived late. I used to leave earlier and earlier, yet I still felt uncertain about reaching the classroom on time. Then a classmate suggested an alternative: walking ten minutes to the train station.

The train journey was slightly longer than a bus journey on a good day. However, its departure times were more predictable. I tried it for two weeks and found that I could plan my evening more calmly. The walk also gave me time to listen to a short podcast.

I still take the bus when the weather is unpleasant and I am not in a hurry. I have not decided that one form of transport is always better. I have simply learned to choose according to what matters most for a particular trip.

questions.prompt: What is the speaker's main point?
options: A transport choice should depend on the needs of the trip.
Walking is always faster than taking a bus.
Train journeys are always shorter than bus journeys.
People should avoid evening classes.
questions.explanation: 结尾总结了因具体行程需求而作选择的想法，而不是断言某种交通工具永远更好。
questions.quote: I have simply learned to choose according to what matters most for a particular trip.

questions.prompt: How long did the speaker try travelling by train?
options: Two days.
One week.
Two weeks.
Several months.
questions.explanation: 说话人尝试新路线的时间是 two weeks，即两周。
questions.quote: I tried it for two weeks and found that I could plan my evening more calmly.

questions.prompt: What mattered most when the speaker chose the train for class?
options: Avoiding all walking.
Being able to plan the arrival time more confidently.
Paying the lowest possible ticket price.
Sitting next to a classmate on every journey.
questions.explanation: 公交的迟到导致不确定性，而火车班次更可预测，因此更可靠地安排到达时间是主要考虑。
questions.quote: However, its departure times were more predictable.

questions.prompt: What is an "alternative" in this situation?
options: A reason to cancel the class.
A type of language exercise.
A warning about the weather.
Another possible choice.
questions.explanation: 同学提出的是原有公交路线之外的另一种可行方式，因此 alternative 表示另一选择。
questions.quote: Then a classmate suggested an alternative: walking ten minutes to the train station.

listening.title: 声音展览的邀请
listening.subtitle: A Gallery You Can Help Create
listening.body:
A small gallery in our neighbourhood is preparing an exhibition about everyday sounds. Instead of displaying only work by professional artists, it has invited local residents to contribute recordings. People can send in sounds from a favourite place, together with a short explanation of why that place matters to them.

I recorded the sound of chairs being moved in the community hall after our weekly music practice. At first, I thought the recording was too ordinary. But the organiser said that ordinary sounds could reveal how people share a space. My explanation helped visitors understand the memory behind it.

The gallery will provide headphones and printed descriptions for each recording. Residents who do not have recording equipment can borrow a simple device during a workshop. The organisers hope the project will encourage people to notice their surroundings and discover stories that would otherwise remain unheard. The exhibition opens next month and admission is free.

questions.prompt: What is special about the planned exhibition?
options: It sells professional recording equipment.
It displays paintings of famous musicians.
It invites residents to share meaningful everyday sounds.
It allows visitors to enter only during music practice.
questions.explanation: 展览邀请当地居民提交日常声音，并解释地点的个人意义，体现了居民参与和声音背后的故事。
questions.quote: People can send in sounds from a favourite place, together with a short explanation of why that place matters to them.

questions.prompt: What sound did the speaker record?
options: Chairs being moved after music practice.
A train leaving a station.
Visitors entering the gallery.
A professional singer performing outdoors.
questions.explanation: 说话人录下的是每周音乐练习后，社区礼堂里挪动椅子的声音。
questions.quote: I recorded the sound of chairs being moved in the community hall after our weekly music practice.

questions.prompt: What does the equipment loan suggest about the project?
options: It expects all residents to buy new devices.
It values expensive recordings more than personal stories.
It plans to stop accepting public recordings.
It tries to make participation easier for more residents.
questions.explanation: 提供可借用的录音设备降低了参与门槛，说明项目希望让更多居民参加。
questions.quote: Residents who do not have recording equipment can borrow a simple device during a workshop.

questions.prompt: What does "contribute recordings" mean here?
options: Delete recordings from a device.
Provide recordings for the project.
Buy recordings from the gallery.
Translate every recording into another language.
questions.explanation: 这里 contribute 后接 recordings，意为向展览项目提供录音材料。
questions.quote: Instead of displaying only work by professional artists, it has invited local residents to contribute recordings.

listening.title: 冰箱门上的晚餐计划
listening.subtitle: Dinner Before the Shopping Trip
listening.body:
Sharing a flat has taught me that buying food is easier than using it. My two flatmates and I used to shop separately. We often bought the same vegetables, then discovered them at the back of the fridge too late. Nobody wanted to waste food, but nobody knew what the others had planned.

Now we keep a small board on the fridge door. Before shopping, we write down ingredients that need to be used soon. Then we choose two evening meals around that list. We leave the other evenings open because our class schedules sometimes change. On Sundays, we cook one larger dish and freeze a few portions for busy days.

The plan is deliberately simple. We are not trying to control every meal. We just want the food we already own to become the starting point for our next shopping trip.

questions.prompt: What is the speaker mainly describing?
options: A simple way to plan meals around food already at home.
A competition to cook the most difficult dishes.
A rule requiring flatmates to eat every meal together.
A decision to stop buying fresh vegetables.
questions.explanation: 说话人介绍先查看已有食材再安排部分晚餐的方法，重点是通过简单计划减少食物浪费。
questions.quote: We just want the food we already own to become the starting point for our next shopping trip.

questions.prompt: What do the flatmates write on the board before shopping?
options: The prices at every nearby food shop.
The names of visitors arriving that week.
Ingredients that need to be used soon.
All the meals they ate the previous month.
questions.explanation: 原文明确说明，他们购物前会把需要尽快使用的食材写在冰箱门上的小板上。
questions.quote: Before shopping, we write down ingredients that need to be used soon.

questions.prompt: Why do they leave some evenings unplanned?
options: They dislike eating anything that has been frozen.
They need room for changes in their daily schedules.
They expect visitors to bring all their dinners.
They have decided never to cook during the week.
questions.explanation: 其余晚餐不固定，是因为课程安排可能变化，可以推知他们希望计划保留调整余地。
questions.quote: We leave the other evenings open because our class schedules sometimes change.

questions.prompt: What does "portions" mean in this talk?
options: Cooking instructions on a food package.
Different rooms inside the shared flat.
Dates when fresh food must be bought.
Amounts of food prepared for individual meals.
questions.explanation: 周日做较大的一道菜，再分装冷冻以备忙碌时食用，所以 portions 指分好的一份份食物。
questions.quote: On Sundays, we cook one larger dish and freeze a few portions for busy days.

listening.title: 安装应用前的一分钟
listening.subtitle: A Moment Before Allowing Access
listening.body:
I downloaded a photo editing app before a weekend trip. During setup, it asked to use my camera, contacts, and location. I nearly accepted everything because I wanted to try its filters quickly. Then I wondered why editing a picture required my address book.

I opened the permission settings and allowed access only to the photographs I selected. The app still worked for the task I needed. Later, a friend pointed out that some features might genuinely require extra access. A location feature, for example, could use my position to suggest nearby photo spots. That did not mean I had to use it.

I now review these requests when I install an app. I ask what a permission enables and whether I need that feature. It takes a little longer than pressing every button immediately, but I feel more aware of the choices I am making.

questions.prompt: What change in behaviour does the speaker describe?
options: Refusing to take photographs during trips.
Downloading several editing apps every weekend.
Checking why an app asks for certain permissions.
Sharing a contact list with every new app.
questions.explanation: 文章从安装应用时险些全部授权讲起，最后说明现在会逐项检查权限的用途和自身需要。
questions.quote: I ask what a permission enables and whether I need that feature.

questions.prompt: What did the speaker initially allow the app to access?
options: Only the photographs the speaker selected.
All the contacts stored on the phone.
The phone's location at every moment.
Every file belonging to the speaker's friend.
questions.explanation: 说话人打开权限设置后，只允许应用访问自己选中的照片，而不是通讯录或持续位置。
questions.quote: I opened the permission settings and allowed access only to the photographs I selected.

questions.prompt: What does the friend's example suggest about permissions?
options: Every requested permission is essential for editing a photo.
An app cannot operate without access to an address book.
Users must always enable nearby photo suggestions.
A permission may support a feature that a user can choose to skip.
questions.explanation: 朋友举出附近拍照地点推荐的例子，随后说话人指出自己不必使用，说明部分权限对应可选功能。
questions.quote: That did not mean I had to use it.

questions.prompt: What does "review" mean in the final paragraph?
options: Advertise an app to a larger group.
Examine something carefully before deciding.
Replace the phone with a newer model.
Copy information without reading it.
questions.explanation: 后一句说明会询问权限能实现什么、是否需要该功能，因此 review 在这里是仔细检查和审视。
questions.quote: I now review these requests when I install an app.

listening.title: 实习第一周的提问本
listening.subtitle: Questions Worth Keeping
listening.body:
During my first week at a publishing company, I kept quiet whenever I did not understand an instruction. I wanted to appear capable, so I guessed what unfamiliar terms meant. By Thursday, I had prepared a list of book prices using the wrong version of a file. Correcting it took much longer than asking would have done.

My supervisor suggested that I keep a question notebook. If a question prevented me from continuing safely, I should ask at once. Other questions could wait until our short afternoon check. She also asked me to explain what I had already tried, so she could understand where I was stuck.

The notebook soon contained fewer repeated questions because I wrote down the answers too. I learned that being independent did not mean knowing everything. It meant recognising what I could solve myself and explaining clearly when I needed guidance.

questions.prompt: What did the speaker learn during the internship?
options: Keeping every difficulty private is the best way to work.
Working independently includes knowing when to ask for help.
A question notebook should contain only technical terms.
Book prices never need to be checked more than once.
questions.explanation: 最后一段把独立工作解释为分清哪些问题能自己解决，哪些需要清楚地向他人寻求指导。
questions.quote: It meant recognising what I could solve myself and explaining clearly when I needed guidance.

questions.prompt: What mistake did the speaker make in the first week?
options: Sending a supervisor's notebook to a customer.
Missing a meeting about book cover designs.
Deleting the company's complete list of books.
Preparing a price list from the wrong file version.
questions.explanation: 文中明确交代，说话人使用错误版本的文件准备了图书价格表，返工比直接提问更费时间。
questions.quote: By Thursday, I had prepared a list of book prices using the wrong version of a file.

questions.prompt: Why did the supervisor ask what the speaker had already tried?
options: To identify the specific point where help was needed.
To avoid answering any questions in the afternoon.
To prove that every mistake came from a difficult file.
To make the speaker repeat the full task from memory.
questions.explanation: 主管希望了解说话人已经尝试了什么及卡在哪里，可推知这样能更有针对性地提供帮助。
questions.quote: She also asked me to explain what I had already tried, so she could understand where I was stuck.

questions.prompt: What does "capable" mean in the first paragraph?
options: Unwilling to listen to instructions.
Interested mainly in earning money.
Having the ability to do a job well.
Recently employed by another company.
questions.explanation: 说话人不懂也不问，是因为想显得能够胜任工作，所以 capable 在这里表示有能力的。
questions.quote: I wanted to appear capable, so I guessed what unfamiliar terms meant.

listening.title: 给夜晚留一个结束点
listening.subtitle: An Ending for the Evening
listening.body:
My evenings used to end whenever my phone battery became low. After finishing my coursework, I would watch one short video, then another. I did not especially enjoy every clip, but there was always something new waiting. In the morning, I often wished I had stopped earlier.

I decided to try a clearer ending to the day. At half past ten, I put my phone on a shelf across the room and chose a quiet activity for the next twenty minutes. Sometimes I read a novel; sometimes I prepared my bag for the following day. I also moved my alarm clock beside the bed, so I no longer needed the phone there.

This routine does not make every evening perfect. When an assignment runs late, I adjust it. Still, having a definite stopping point makes it easier to notice when I am continuing out of habit rather than interest.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of the speaker's new routine?
options: To finish every assignment before dinner.
To watch as many short videos as possible.
To use a phone as the only alarm clock.
To create a clear point for ending evening phone use.
questions.explanation: 新习惯围绕固定时间把手机放远并安排安静活动展开，其目的是给无休止的晚间刷视频设定结束点。
questions.quote: I decided to try a clearer ending to the day.

questions.prompt: Where does the speaker put the phone at half past ten?
options: Inside a bag beside the front door.
On a shelf across the room.
Under a pillow on the bed.
Next to a new clock on the desk.
questions.explanation: 原文明确说十点半把手机放在房间另一边的架子上，因此不是放在床边或枕头下面。
questions.quote: At half past ten, I put my phone on a shelf across the room and chose a quiet activity for the next twenty minutes.

questions.prompt: What can be inferred about the speaker's approach to the routine?
options: The speaker follows it only when the phone battery is empty.
The speaker expects it to solve every difficulty immediately.
The speaker allows changes when other responsibilities require them.
The speaker has decided to stop doing coursework in the evening.
questions.explanation: 说话人提到作业结束较晚时会调整，可见这个习惯保留了根据实际责任改变的余地。
questions.quote: When an assignment runs late, I adjust it.

questions.prompt: What does "definite" mean in the final sentence?
options: Clear and firmly identified.
Expensive to arrange.
Chosen by somebody else.
Impossible to remember.
questions.explanation: 固定时间收起手机为晚间活动提供了清楚的边界，因此 definite 在这里表示明确、确定的。
questions.quote: Still, having a definite stopping point makes it easier to notice when I am continuing out of habit rather than interest.

listening.title: 一家老面包店的故事
listening.subtitle: The Story Behind the Bakery
listening.body:
For a local history assignment, I interviewed the owner of a bakery near our college. I arrived with questions about dates and building changes. However, the most interesting part came when she described learning to bake from her aunt, who judged the oven's heat by holding a hand near its door.

I asked whether I could record the interview and explained that it would be used in a class presentation. Afterwards, I sent her a written version to check. She corrected the year the shop had moved and asked me to remove a personal story about a neighbour. I made both changes before sharing the work.

The experience taught me that an interview is more than collecting colourful memories. People should understand how their words will be used. Checking details also helps separate a lively story from an accurate account, although both can help us understand a place.

questions.prompt: What is the speaker's main lesson from the interview?
options: Good interviews require both respect for the speaker and care with facts.
Personal memories should always replace historical dates.
Every interesting story can be shared without asking.
Written accounts are unnecessary in a history project.
questions.explanation: 文章既强调征求录音和使用同意，也强调核对年份与删去私人故事，说明尊重受访者和事实准确同样重要。
questions.quote: People should understand how their words will be used.

questions.prompt: What did the bakery owner ask the student to remove?
options: Every description of the bakery's old oven.
The name of the college history course.
A personal story about a neighbour.
The entire account of learning from her aunt.
questions.explanation: 受访者检查文字稿时，要求删去的是一段关于邻居的私人故事，学生在分享前照做了。
questions.quote: She corrected the year the shop had moved and asked me to remove a personal story about a neighbour.

questions.prompt: Why was sending the written version useful?
options: It removed the need to ask any interview questions.
It gave the owner a chance to correct facts and set personal limits.
It allowed the student to avoid preparing a class presentation.
It proved that the bakery had never changed its location.
questions.explanation: 文字稿使店主纠正搬店年份并提出删除私人故事的要求，可推知它兼顾事实核对与使用边界。
questions.quote: Afterwards, I sent her a written version to check.

questions.prompt: What does "account" mean in the final sentence?
options: A place for keeping money in a bank.
A password for entering a website.
A total number of bakery customers.
A spoken or written description of events.
questions.explanation: 这里讨论活泼的故事与准确的历史记录，account 指事件的叙述，而不是银行或网站账户。
questions.quote: Checking details also helps separate a lively story from an accurate account, although both can help us understand a place.

listening.title: 新手也能加入的球赛
listening.subtitle: A Game with Room for Beginners
listening.body:
Our weekend volleyball group almost disappeared last term. Experienced players wanted a fast game, while beginners hardly touched the ball. A few new members stopped coming, and soon there were not enough people for two teams. The problem was not a lack of interest in exercise. It was the way our sessions were organised.

This term, we begin with fifteen minutes of paired practice. Each beginner works with someone who can explain the basic movements. We then play a friendly game with mixed teams. Players can choose a more competitive session later in the afternoon, but nobody has to stay for it.

I enjoy the arrangement because it gives me a chance to improve without feeling that every mistake ruins the game. Our strongest players still have a challenge, and newcomers have a reason to return. Sharing a sport works better when people can enter at different levels.

questions.prompt: What is the talk mainly about?
options: Why volleyball should be replaced with another sport.
How the group selects only its strongest players.
How different session levels help more people enjoy volleyball.
Why every friendly game should last an entire afternoon.
questions.explanation: 新安排包括基础结对练习、混合友谊赛和可选竞技场次，主旨是让不同水平的人都能参加排球活动。
questions.quote: Sharing a sport works better when people can enter at different levels.

questions.prompt: How does the volleyball session begin this term?
options: With fifteen minutes of paired practice.
With a written test about the rules.
With an hour reserved for experienced players.
With a competition between two beginner teams.
questions.explanation: 第二段明确说明，新学期每次活动以十五分钟的结对练习开始，由有经验者帮助新手。
questions.quote: This term, we begin with fifteen minutes of paired practice.

questions.prompt: Why are newcomers more likely to return now?
options: They are promised a place on a professional team.
They never need to practise difficult movements.
They can prevent experienced players from competing.
They can learn and participate without facing only a fast game.
questions.explanation: 新手获得基础指导，并能在混合友谊赛中练习，不再只能面对高强度比赛，因此更有理由继续参加。
questions.quote: I enjoy the arrangement because it gives me a chance to improve without feeling that every mistake ruins the game.

questions.prompt: What does "competitive" mean when describing the later session?
options: Designed mainly for silent observation.
Focused more strongly on trying to win.
Available only to people teaching the sport.
Unrelated to the rules of volleyball.
questions.explanation: 后面的场次与前面的友谊赛相对应，competitive 表示更注重较量和争取胜利的竞技性活动。
questions.quote: Players can choose a more competitive session later in the afternoon, but nobody has to stay for it.

listening.title: 每月自动扣费的清单
listening.subtitle: The Small Payments on My Statement
listening.body:
When I checked my monthly spending, I was surprised by several small payments I barely remembered. A music service was useful, but I also paid for a drawing app I had opened only once. A free trial for a magazine had ended while I was busy with exams, and regular payments had begun.

I made a list of every subscription, its renewal date, and how often I used it. I cancelled the ones that no longer served a purpose. For a service I wanted to keep, I added a reminder before the next payment so I could reconsider it. I did not cancel everything just to make the list shorter.

This exercise helped me see a difference between an affordable price and a useful purchase. A small charge can still be unnecessary. Now, before starting a free trial, I check how to cancel it and put the ending date in my calendar.

questions.prompt: What is the speaker's main point about small regular payments?
options: Every paid digital service should be replaced by a free one.
They should be reviewed according to whether they remain useful.
A low price always makes a subscription worth keeping.
They can be understood without looking at payment dates.
questions.explanation: 说话人逐项检查订阅是否仍有用途，并保留有用的项目，强调不能只因为单次价格低就继续付款。
questions.quote: This exercise helped me see a difference between an affordable price and a useful purchase.

questions.prompt: Which service had the speaker opened only once?
options: A music service used for daily listening.
A calendar for tracking exam dates.
A magazine website recommended in class.
A drawing app that required payment.
questions.explanation: 第一段明确说，说话人为一个只打开过一次的绘画应用付费，这是清单中被忽视的开支之一。
questions.quote: A music service was useful, but I also paid for a drawing app I had opened only once.

questions.prompt: Why does the speaker add a reminder before a future payment?
options: To have time to decide whether the service is still worth keeping.
To ensure that every subscription becomes more expensive.
To prevent any paid service from being used during exams.
To avoid knowing when free trials will end.
questions.explanation: 说话人设置付款前提醒，是为了届时重新考虑是否保留服务，而不是不加检查地让它续费。
questions.quote: For a service I wanted to keep, I added a reminder before the next payment so I could reconsider it.

questions.prompt: What does "affordable" mean in this talk?
options: Guaranteed to be used every day.
Provided without any conditions.
Within the amount someone can pay.
Designed only for professional artists.
questions.explanation: 文章区分价格是否承担得起和购买是否有用，因此 affordable 指价格在个人支付能力范围之内。
questions.quote: This exercise helped me see a difference between an affordable price and a useful purchase.

listening.title: 看鸟时学会保留问号
listening.subtitle: Leaving Space for an Uncertain Bird
listening.body:
I joined a birdwatching walk because I wanted to learn the names of birds in our park. Our guide asked us to watch quietly from the path and avoid moving close to nests. She said a good view was never a reason to disturb an animal.

At the lake, I saw a small brown bird and immediately chose a name from my guidebook. Another member asked about its tail and the way it moved. I had not noticed either detail. Instead of agreeing with my first guess, the guide suggested writing down what I could actually see and marking the name as uncertain.

Since then, I have kept short notes about size, movement, and location before checking pictures. Some birds remain unnamed in my notebook, and that is acceptable. I am learning to observe more patiently. An honest question mark can be more useful than a confident label based on a quick glance.

questions.prompt: What lesson does the speaker learn from birdwatching?
options: A bird's name matters more than how it behaves.
Guidebooks remove every need for careful observation.
Walking closer always produces more reliable information.
Careful observation includes admitting when an identification is uncertain.
questions.explanation: 说话人从急于给鸟命名转向先记录特征，并接受暂时不能确定名称，强调认真观察与承认不确定性。
questions.quote: An honest question mark can be more useful than a confident label based on a quick glance.

questions.prompt: Where did the guide ask the group to watch birds from?
options: The area directly beneath each nest.
The path through the park.
A boat in the middle of the lake.
The roof of a nearby building.
questions.explanation: 导游开头要求大家留在小路上安静观看，并避免靠近鸟巢，以减少对动物的干扰。
questions.quote: Our guide asked us to watch quietly from the path and avoid moving close to nests.

questions.prompt: Why did the guide suggest marking the bird's name as uncertain?
options: She did not want anyone to use a guidebook.
The park had stopped allowing bird names in notebooks.
The speaker had missed features needed to support the first guess.
She believed that all small brown birds had the same name.
questions.explanation: 同伴询问尾巴和移动方式时，说话人发现自己都未观察，这表明最初命名缺少足够特征依据。
questions.quote: I had not noticed either detail.

questions.prompt: What does "glance" mean in the final sentence?
options: A brief and quick look.
A detailed written report.
A loud sound made by a bird.
A planned walk lasting all day.
questions.explanation: 结尾将耐心观察与根据快速一眼就自信命名作比较，因此 glance 指短暂、匆忙的一瞥。
questions.quote: An honest question mark can be more useful than a confident label based on a quick glance.

listening.title: 菜单里的文化解释
listening.subtitle: More Than a Word on a Menu
listening.body:
Our language club helped prepare an English menu for a student food festival. We expected the job to be simple: find the English words and type them beside the original names. Then we reached a dish whose name referred to a local story rather than its ingredients. A direct translation sounded interesting but gave visitors no idea what they would eat.

We decided to keep the traditional name and add a short description of the main ingredients and cooking method. We checked these descriptions with the student cooks, especially where a dish might contain nuts or dairy products. There was limited space, so we removed long historical notes and placed them on a separate page.

Translating the menu became an exercise in choosing what readers needed first. We wanted to preserve the dishes' cultural identity while helping visitors make informed choices. Sometimes a useful explanation does more work than a single translated word.

questions.prompt: What did the club learn from translating the menu?
options: Useful translation should consider both cultural meaning and readers' practical needs.
Every dish should be given an entirely new English name.
Readers need historical stories before any ingredient information.
A direct word translation always explains what a dish contains.
questions.explanation: 团队保留传统名称又补充食材和做法说明，目的是兼顾文化身份与读者选择食物时的实际需要。
questions.quote: We wanted to preserve the dishes' cultural identity while helping visitors make informed choices.

questions.prompt: Where did the club put the longer historical notes?
options: On labels attached to the cooks' clothes.
Under every ingredient in the main menu.
On a separate page.
Inside the festival ticket envelope.
questions.explanation: 原文说明由于菜单空间有限，团队把较长的历史背景说明移到了另一页。
questions.quote: There was limited space, so we removed long historical notes and placed them on a separate page.

questions.prompt: Why did the club check the descriptions with the cooks?
options: To ask the cooks to invent a new local story.
To make sure important food information was accurate.
To prevent visitors from reading the traditional dish names.
To replace every dish containing dairy with a dessert.
questions.explanation: 他们特别核对坚果和乳制品等成分，可推知目的是保证影响食物选择的重要信息准确。
questions.quote: We checked these descriptions with the student cooks, especially where a dish might contain nuts or dairy products.

questions.prompt: What does "preserve" mean in the final paragraph?
options: Change something beyond recognition.
Hide information from all readers.
Make a dish last longer in a freezer.
Keep an important quality or feature.
questions.explanation: 这里的对象是菜肴的文化身份，保留传统名称就是保存其重要特征，因此 preserve 意为保留。
questions.quote: We wanted to preserve the dishes' cultural identity while helping visitors make informed choices.

listening.title: 寄错包裹之后
listening.subtitle: Putting a Delivery Mistake Right
listening.body:
I help a small student business pack handmade notebooks. Last month, two customers received each other's orders because I had placed the wrong labels on their boxes. My first thought was to explain how busy we had been. Then I realised that this would not help either customer get the notebook they wanted.

I contacted them separately, described the mistake, and offered a clear plan. We would pay for returning the incorrect notebooks and send the right ones without waiting for those returns. I gave each customer a date for the replacement and checked that the address was correct.

Both customers accepted the plan. Afterwards, our team introduced a final check in which a second person compares the order number with the label. I still feel embarrassed about the error, but I understand responsibility differently now. It includes explaining what happened, repairing the problem, and changing the process that allowed it.

questions.prompt: What is the speaker mainly explaining?
options: Why a student business stopped selling notebooks.
How to make handmade notebooks at a lower cost.
How taking responsibility led to fixing and preventing an order mistake.
Why customers should always check labels before paying.
questions.explanation: 全文从贴错标签讲到补发、承担退货费用和增加核对程序，重点是通过实际行动承担责任。
questions.quote: It includes explaining what happened, repairing the problem, and changing the process that allowed it.

questions.prompt: When would the business send the correct notebooks?
options: Before waiting for the incorrect notebooks to be returned.
Only after the customers paid a second delivery fee.
After every notebook in the shop had been sold.
Only if the customers collected them in person.
questions.explanation: 补救计划明确说明，不必等寄错的笔记本退回就先发出正确商品，而且由店家承担退货费用。
questions.quote: We would pay for returning the incorrect notebooks and send the right ones without waiting for those returns.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of the second person's final check?
options: To judge which notebook design is most attractive.
To make every customer order two notebooks.
To remove order numbers from future packages.
To catch a mismatch before a package is sent.
questions.explanation: 第二个人会把订单号与标签核对，可推知其作用是在包裹寄出前发现标签与订单不一致。
questions.quote: Afterwards, our team introduced a final check in which a second person compares the order number with the label.

questions.prompt: What does "replacement" mean in this talk?
options: A written explanation of why a shop is busy.
An item supplied in place of an incorrect one.
An extra charge added to a customer's payment.
A box that the customer must keep unopened.
questions.explanation: 顾客收到了错误商品，因此 replacement 指店家随后提供、用来代替错误笔记本的正确商品。
questions.quote: I gave each customer a date for the replacement and checked that the address was correct.

listening.title: 假期里的校园花园
listening.subtitle: A Garden That Could Survive the Holiday
listening.body:
Our campus gardening club wanted to fill a sunny courtyard with flowers. We chose colourful plants from a catalogue and imagined how the space would look in spring. A member then asked a question we had forgotten: who would water the garden during the summer holiday? Most of us would be away.

We spoke to the grounds staff before buying anything. They helped us choose plants suited to the local conditions and explained which ones needed frequent care. We reduced the planting area and covered the soil around the plants to help keep moisture in. A nearby department agreed to include the remaining watering in its summer duties.

The finished garden is smaller than our first design, but it has a realistic care plan. I used to think a successful garden began with attractive plants. Now I also think about what those plants will need after the opening photographs have been taken.

questions.prompt: What is the main lesson of the gardening project?
options: A large planting area always requires less work.
A garden design must account for continuing care as well as appearance.
Summer watering can be ignored if plants look attractive in spring.
Students should select flowers only from photographs.
questions.explanation: 团队发现假期无人浇水的问题后调整植物和面积，并安排后续维护，说明设计必须考虑持续照料。
questions.quote: The finished garden is smaller than our first design, but it has a realistic care plan.

questions.prompt: Why did the club cover the soil around the plants?
options: To hide the plants from courtyard visitors.
To create more space for an opening ceremony.
To stop the grounds staff from checking the garden.
To help keep moisture in the soil.
questions.explanation: 第二段明确说，覆盖植物周围的土壤是为了帮助保持水分，属于减少养护压力的措施。
questions.quote: We reduced the planting area and covered the soil around the plants to help keep moisture in.

questions.prompt: Why did the club consult the grounds staff before buying plants?
options: The staff could help match the design to practical growing conditions.
The staff wanted to replace the courtyard with a car park.
The club had decided that no flowers could grow in sunlight.
The catalogue already included a complete summer care team.
questions.explanation: 工作人员帮助选择适应当地条件的植物并解释养护频率，可推知咨询使设计更符合现实种植条件。
questions.quote: They helped us choose plants suited to the local conditions and explained which ones needed frequent care.

questions.prompt: What does "realistic" mean when describing the care plan?
options: Based entirely on an imaginary garden.
Designed mainly to impress visitors in photographs.
Practical and possible to carry out.
Required to remain unchanged in every season.
questions.explanation: 缩小面积、选择合适植物并落实假期浇水人员后，计划能够真正执行，因此 realistic 表示切实可行。
questions.quote: The finished garden is smaller than our first design, but it has a realistic care plan.

listening.title: 演讲中的停顿
listening.subtitle: Making Space Between Ideas
listening.body:
Before a class presentation, I practised until I could deliver the whole talk without stopping. I thought a pause would make me sound unprepared. During rehearsal, however, my partner said that the ideas arrived so quickly she could not tell which ones mattered most.

She suggested marking three places in my notes where I would pause briefly. One came after the opening question, another before the main example, and the last before the conclusion. At first, those moments of silence felt much longer to me than they sounded in a recording. I also removed two extra examples so the audience would have less to remember.

On the day, I did lose one sentence, but the marked pauses helped me find my place again. My goal had changed. I was no longer trying to prove that I remembered every word. I was trying to give listeners enough time to follow an idea.

questions.prompt: What did the speaker learn about giving a presentation?
options: Remembering every word is the only measure of success.
A presentation should include every example available.
Silence always makes a speaker seem unprepared.
Well-placed pauses can help listeners follow the ideas.
questions.explanation: 说话人从追求毫不停顿地背完，转向在重要位置停顿，目的是给听众留出理解思路的时间。
questions.quote: I was trying to give listeners enough time to follow an idea.

questions.prompt: Where was one of the three planned pauses placed?
options: In the middle of the speaker's name.
Immediately after the opening question.
After every word in the final sentence.
Before the audience entered the classroom.
questions.explanation: 第二段列出三个停顿位置，第一个就在开场问题之后，另两个在主要例子和结论之前。
questions.quote: One came after the opening question, another before the main example, and the last before the conclusion.

questions.prompt: What did listening to the recording help the speaker realise?
options: The partner had removed all the examples without permission.
The talk could be understood only when it contained no silence.
A pause felt longer to the speaker than it sounded to a listener.
The audience would prefer a much longer presentation.
questions.explanation: 说话人发现停顿在自己的感觉中比录音听起来长，可推知录音帮助其校正对沉默时长的判断。
questions.quote: At first, those moments of silence felt much longer to me than they sounded in a recording.

questions.prompt: What does "deliver" mean in the first sentence?
options: Present a talk to listeners.
Carry a package to a home.
Write a list of classroom rules.
Choose a subject for a partner.
questions.explanation: deliver 在这里的宾语是 the whole talk，语境为课堂展示，所以意思是发表或讲出演讲。
questions.quote: Before a class presentation, I practised until I could deliver the whole talk without stopping.

listening.title: 找回照片之前先整理
listening.subtitle: Giving Digital Memories an Order
listening.body:
My family asked me to collect photographs for my grandmother's birthday. I thought I could finish in an afternoon, but our pictures were spread across old phones, messages, and several computers. Many files had names that told me nothing about their contents. Finding one beach photograph took nearly an hour.

I began by copying the pictures into folders organised by year and event. I kept the original files and changed names only in the new collection. Relatives helped identify people and places, and I left a note whenever we were unsure of a date. Finally, I saved another copy on a separate drive and checked that it opened correctly.

The birthday slideshow was only part of the result. We now have a collection that another family member can understand. Organising digital memories is not just about keeping files. It is also about keeping enough context for those files to mean something later.

questions.prompt: What is the main point of the talk?
options: Digital memories need useful organisation and background information.
Every family photograph should be printed immediately.
Old phones are the best place to keep the only copy of a file.
A birthday slideshow should contain no dates or names.
questions.explanation: 说话人不仅归档照片，还补充人物地点和不确定日期的说明，强调让未来的人能理解这些资料。
questions.quote: It is also about keeping enough context for those files to mean something later.

questions.prompt: How did the speaker organise the new photograph folders?
options: By the brand of camera used for each picture.
By the length of the original file names.
By year and event.
By the amount of space left on each phone.
questions.explanation: 原文明确说，新的照片文件夹按照年份和事件来组织，而不是按相机品牌或文件名长度分类。
questions.quote: I began by copying the pictures into folders organised by year and event.

questions.prompt: Why did the speaker leave notes beside uncertain dates?
options: To make relatives choose a date without checking.
To avoid presenting a guess as a confirmed fact.
To stop other family members from opening the files.
To replace the need for a separate saved copy.
questions.explanation: 不确定时留下备注，能够让后来查看者知道哪些日期尚未核实，避免把猜测误认为确定事实。
questions.quote: Relatives helped identify people and places, and I left a note whenever we were unsure of a date.

questions.prompt: What does "context" mean in the final sentence?
options: The electrical power needed by a computer.
The decorative style of a digital slideshow.
The number of unused folders on a drive.
Background details that help people understand something.
questions.explanation: 前文补充人物、地点和日期，正是帮助理解照片的背景信息，因此 context 在这里不是文件大小等技术信息。
questions.quote: It is also about keeping enough context for those files to mean something later.

listening.title: 一锅汤带来的熟悉感
listening.subtitle: A Taste of Home in a Shared Kitchen
listening.body:
When I moved abroad for a term, the hardest moments were often quiet evenings in the residence hall. I enjoyed my classes, but I missed the ordinary conversations that used to happen while my family prepared dinner. One weekend, I called my father and asked how to make his vegetable soup.

Some ingredients were unavailable in the nearby shop, so he suggested substitutes rather than a trip across the city. As the soup cooked, two students from my floor came into the shared kitchen. They asked what I was making, and I offered them a bowl. The next week, one of them taught us to prepare a simple dish from her hometown.

Our small cooking evenings have become a pleasant part of the week. They do not remove every feeling of homesickness. They give us a familiar activity through which we can exchange stories and begin to feel connected in a new place.

vocabulary.meaning: 有联系的；有归属联系的

questions.prompt: What does the speaker mainly describe?
options: A plan to open a restaurant near a residence hall.
A difficult search for every traditional soup ingredient.
How shared cooking helped students build connections abroad.
Why studying abroad made family conversations unnecessary.
questions.explanation: 文章由想念家庭做饭时的交流，讲到共享厨房中的小型聚餐，重点是借熟悉活动建立新的人际联系。
questions.quote: They give us a familiar activity through which we can exchange stories and begin to feel connected in a new place.

questions.prompt: What did the speaker's father suggest when some ingredients were unavailable?
options: Using substitutes for the missing ingredients.
Travelling across the city before cooking.
Waiting until the following term to make soup.
Ordering every ingredient from the hometown.
questions.explanation: 父亲没有建议跨城寻找食材，而是推荐可以替代的原料，让说话人能用附近可得的材料做汤。
questions.quote: Some ingredients were unavailable in the nearby shop, so he suggested substitutes rather than a trip across the city.

questions.prompt: What can be inferred about the students' cooking evenings?
options: They are compulsory events organised by their teachers.
They depend on everyone coming from the same hometown.
They have ended all contact between students and their families.
They create a relaxed setting for learning about one another.
questions.explanation: 大家轮流分享家乡菜并交流故事，可推知这些做饭之夜提供了自然、放松的相互了解机会。
questions.quote: The next week, one of them taught us to prepare a simple dish from her hometown.

questions.prompt: What are "substitutes" in this situation?
options: People hired to cook in a student kitchen.
Ingredients used in place of other ingredients.
Instructions written in several languages.
Dishes that can only be served cold.
questions.explanation: 一些原料买不到时，父亲建议使用能代替它们的材料，因此 substitutes 指这里的替代食材。
questions.quote: Some ingredients were unavailable in the nearby shop, so he suggested substitutes rather than a trip across the city.

listening.title: 舞台旁的字幕屏
listening.subtitle: Words Beside the Stage
listening.body:
Our student theatre group is preparing a short play with captions displayed beside the stage. We began the project after a classmate explained that she could hear parts of a performance but often missed quiet lines. Simply making the actors speak louder would not solve every difficulty.

Two volunteers now work from the final script. They divide the dialogue into short sections and practise displaying each section at the right moment. Important sounds, such as a door closing offstage, are described as well. During a rehearsal, we invited our classmate to sit in several different rows. From the side seats, the first screen was difficult to read, so we changed its position and enlarged the letters.

Preparing captions has required extra work and careful timing. It has also made us think about the audience more closely. An invitation to a performance means more when people have a practical way to follow what happens.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of the theatre group's project?
options: To replace the actors with a set of recorded voices.
To help more audience members follow the performance through captions.

listening.title: 捐衣前的整理工作
listening.subtitle: A Donation That Others Can Use
listening.body:
When our student union announced a clothing collection, I filled a bag with everything I no longer wore. I felt pleased until a volunteer explained the sorting rules. A donation was not simply a way to empty my cupboard. The clothes had to be useful to the people receiving them.

At home, I checked each item again. I washed the jackets, repaired a loose button, and put pairs of socks together. A badly torn shirt went into a separate textile recycling bag because the collection could not accept it. I also read the request carefully: the organisation needed warm everyday clothing, not formal evening wear.

When I returned, the volunteer could sort my bag quickly. I had given fewer items, but they matched the current request. The experience changed how I think about helping. Before offering something, it is worth asking whether it fits the recipient's needs and whether any preparation is still required.

listening.title: 实验记录不只是结果
listening.subtitle: Notes That Let Someone Repeat the Work
listening.body:
In our introductory science class, we compared how different paper shapes affected the distance a small paper glider travelled. My partner and I recorded only the longest flight for each shape. We thought those numbers would make a clear report, but another pair could not repeat our results.

Our teacher asked how high we had held the glider, where we had released it, and whether the windows were open. We had written down none of these conditions. For the next session, we marked a release point, closed the windows, and recorded every attempt, including short flights. We also noted when a wing became bent and replaced the damaged glider.

The new report was less dramatic, but it explained our procedure much better. We could discuss why attempts differed instead of hiding the differences. I learned that useful experimental notes should help another person understand what was done, not merely admire the final result.

listening.title: 陶杯口沿的一次练习
listening.subtitle: Learning One Small Part of a Craft
listening.body:
At my first pottery workshop, I imagined taking home a beautiful cup. Instead, the clay leaned to one side whenever I tried to shape it. I kept changing my hand position, hoping that one quick movement would solve everything. The instructor watched for a moment and then gave me a smaller goal.

She asked me to make the rim even before worrying about the whole cup. I practised that single movement on several pieces of clay. After each attempt, she pointed to one area and asked what I felt under my fingers. Gradually, I began to notice changes in thickness before I could see them clearly.

My final cup was still uneven, but I understood one part of the process better. I signed up for another session with a different expectation. Progress in a craft may begin with learning to notice a small difference, rather than producing a finished object that looks impressive.

listening.title: 校车临时换站
listening.subtitle: A Temporary Bus Stop

The opening of a new science course.
A temporary change to a bus stop.
The cancellation of every campus bus.

On Thursday.
On Monday.
On Tuesday.

Signs leading to the lower entrance.
A notice about buying a new ticket.

listening.subtitle: The Swap Shelf

You may leave clean books, working kitchen tools, or unused notebooks, and take something useful in return. Please do not bring food or electrical devices, since volunteers cannot check their safety. You do not have to exchange items of equal value. The aim is to keep useful things in use, not to run a shop. Volunteers inspect the shelf each Friday and donate any suitable items that have remained there for a month.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of the swap shelf?

To help people reuse useful objects.
To compare the prices of new books.
To collect food for a restaurant.
questions.explanation: 说话人明确指出目的是让有用物品继续被使用，交换角并不是一家以赚钱为目的的商店。
questions.quote: The aim is to keep useful things in use, not to run a shop.

questions.prompt: Which item can people leave on the shelf?

A broken kitchen tool.
An old electric heater.
A bag of fresh food.

listening.title: 午间十分钟

questions.quote: Last month, I began taking a ten-minute walk after lunch without my phone.

questions.quote: On rainy days, I walk along the covered corridor instead of going outside.

listening.title: 给手机充电的规矩

reading.title: 菜园里的公平
reading.subtitle: Sharing More Than a Garden
reading.body:
When a group of students turned an empty piece of campus land into a garden, they expected their main challenge to be keeping the plants alive. They soon discovered that sharing the work was more complicated than choosing vegetables. Some members could visit every morning, while others had classes or paid jobs at that time.

At first, the group gave the most convenient growing spaces to whoever arrived earliest. The rule appeared fair because it was the same for everyone. In practice, however, it rewarded people whose schedules already allowed them to come early. Several enthusiastic members stopped attending because they felt they had little influence over the garden.

Rather than blame these members for lacking commitment, the organisers asked them what needed to change. They introduced a rotating schedule to allocate the growing spaces. They also created an evening work session once a week. Members could contribute in other ways, such as keeping records, designing signs, or arranging the collection of tools. Each task was listed publicly, so less visible work could be recognised.

The changes did not remove every disagreement. Some students still preferred the old arrangement, and the organisers reviewed the schedule after a month. Yet participation became more varied, and people who had almost left began returning. The garden produced vegetables, but its more important achievement was a better process for working together. The group learned that a shared project needs more than one rule that looks equal on paper. It also needs attention to the different circumstances in which people try to take part.

questions.prompt: What is the main message of the passage?
options: Student gardens should grow only easy vegetables.
Fair cooperation requires attention to people's different circumstances.
Early arrival is the best measure of commitment.
Shared projects work best without written rules.
questions.explanation: 文章以先到先得规则造成的参与差异为起点，说明合作中的公平还需要考虑参与者的不同条件。
questions.quote: It also needs attention to the different circumstances in which people try to take part.

questions.prompt: Which change did the organisers make?
options: They required every member to visit each morning.
They gave all growing spaces to the earliest visitors.
They stopped recognising work done outside the garden.
They added a weekly evening work session.
questions.explanation: 原文明确写到每周增加一次晚间劳动时段，以便不方便早到的人参加。
questions.quote: They also created an evening work session once a week.

questions.prompt: Why did some enthusiastic members stop attending at first?
options: The original system limited their ability to influence the project.
They discovered that vegetables could not grow on campus.
The organisers refused to publish any information about tasks.
They had already completed all the work required of them.
questions.explanation: 先到者长期获得便利地块，使其他成员觉得自己缺少影响力；这与是否热心并非同一件事。
questions.quote: Several enthusiastic members stopped attending because they felt they had little influence over the garden.

questions.prompt: What does "allocate" mean in the third paragraph?
options: Measure the temperature of.
Remove plants from.
Distribute for people to use.
Advertise for sale.
questions.explanation: 轮换安排的作用是把种植地块分配给成员使用，因此 allocate 表示分配。
questions.quote: They introduced a rotating schedule to allocate the growing spaces.

reading.title: 让反馈真正有用
reading.subtitle: Feedback That Leads Somewhere
reading.body:
During her first month at a publishing company, Maya received several comments saying that her reports needed to be more professional. She wanted to improve, but the advice left her uncertain. Did professional mean shorter sentences, fewer personal opinions, or a different way of arranging information? The word described a goal without showing her a route towards it.

Her supervisor noticed the problem and changed their next discussion. Instead of giving another general judgement, he selected one paragraph from a recent report. He pointed out that its central recommendation appeared only in the final sentence. Together, they moved that sentence to the beginning and checked whether the supporting information followed logically. Maya could now see a specific change that made the paragraph easier to understand.

They agreed to focus on one writing feature each week. Maya would revise an example, explain the reason for her changes, and then try the same approach in a new report. The supervisor also asked which parts of the feedback she found difficult to apply. This gave him information about his own explanations, rather than treating all confusion as a weakness in her work.

After several weeks, Maya still made mistakes, but she was less dependent on someone correcting every line. She had begun asking useful questions while writing. Is my main point clear? Does this detail support it? Helpful feedback had become a tool she could use for herself. The experience suggests that advice is valuable not simply because it identifies a problem, but because it helps a person decide what to do next and understand why that action may work.

questions.prompt: What makes feedback useful, according to the passage?
options: It lists every possible mistake at the same time.
It relies on general labels that sound professional.
It gives understandable next steps and the reasons behind them.
It allows the supervisor to rewrite every report completely.
questions.explanation: 结尾总结了有用反馈的两个要素：帮助人决定下一步做什么，并理解为什么这样做。
questions.quote: The experience suggests that advice is valuable not simply because it identifies a problem, but because it helps a person decide what to do next and understand why that action may work.

questions.prompt: What did Maya and her supervisor do to improve the example paragraph?
options: They moved its central recommendation to the beginning.
They removed every sentence containing an opinion.
They changed all its words into technical terms.
They placed the supporting information in a separate report.
questions.explanation: 主管指出核心建议出现在末句，随后二人将这句话移到开头，并检查后文的逻辑。
questions.quote: Together, they moved that sentence to the beginning and checked whether the supporting information followed logically.

questions.prompt: What does the supervisor's question about difficult feedback show?
options: He expected Maya to understand every instruction immediately.
He believed confusion could never result from his explanations.
He wanted Maya to stop asking for help.
He regarded feedback as a process that could improve on both sides.
questions.explanation: 他询问哪些建议难以落实，以检查自己的解释，说明反馈是可以双向改进的过程。
questions.quote: This gave him information about his own explanations, rather than treating all confusion as a weakness in her work.

questions.prompt: What does "specific" mean in "a specific change"?
options: A change made without a clear purpose.
A clearly identified, particular change.
A change suitable for every report in exactly the same way.
A change that must remain secret.
questions.explanation: 这里指把核心建议移到开头这一明确可操作的改动，所以 specific 是具体明确的。
questions.quote: Maya could now see a specific change that made the paragraph easier to understand.

reading.title: 环保选择为何没有被选择
reading.subtitle: Making the Reusable Choice Easier
reading.body:
A student newspaper wanted to understand why reusable cups were rarely chosen at a campus cafe. The cafe already offered a small discount to customers who brought their own cups. Posters near the counter explained the offer, yet most drinks were still served in disposable containers. It was tempting to conclude that students simply did not care about waste.

Before writing that conclusion, the newspaper team interviewed customers. Some had left their cups in their rooms. Others were unsure whether staff would accept a cup that was not the cafe's official model. Several students said they avoided carrying a dirty cup after finishing a drink. These answers pointed to practical obstacles rather than a single lack of concern.

With permission from the cafe, the team tested a small change for two weeks. A shelf near the entrance displayed clean cups that customers could borrow and return later. A clear sign said that any suitable personal cup was welcome. Staff also explained where borrowed cups should be returned. The idea was to make the reusable choice more convenient during an ordinary busy day.

The team recorded more use of reusable cups during the trial. However, it did not claim that the change would have the same result everywhere. The trial was short, and customers knew that a student project was taking place. The newspaper reported both the increase and these limitations. Its strongest conclusion was modest: before judging people's values from their choices, look carefully at the conditions under which those choices are made. A useful improvement may begin with removing a small difficulty that a poster alone cannot solve.

questions.prompt: What is the central idea of the passage?
options: Removing practical obstacles can help people make a preferred choice.
Discounts always prevent waste without other changes.
A short trial can prove that one policy works everywhere.
Students' choices are explained entirely by their personal values.
questions.explanation: 文章通过访谈和试行说明，应先检查实际障碍，不能只凭选择结果判断人们是否在意环保。
questions.quote: A useful improvement may begin with removing a small difficulty that a poster alone cannot solve.

questions.prompt: What did the team add near the entrance during the trial?
options: A machine selling disposable cups.
A desk for collecting student opinions only.
A shelf of clean cups available to borrow.
A sign accepting only the cafe's official cup model.
questions.explanation: 试行方案在入口附近放置了一架干净杯子，供顾客借用并稍后归还。
questions.quote: A shelf near the entrance displayed clean cups that customers could borrow and return later.

questions.prompt: Why did the newspaper mention the trial's limitations?
options: To suggest that no observations had been collected.
To avoid making a broader claim than the evidence supported.
To argue that all customer interviews were dishonest.
To prove that reusable cups could never become popular.
questions.explanation: 试行时间短、顾客知道项目存在，这些条件限制了结论的适用范围，报告局限是为了避免过度推广结果。
questions.quote: However, it did not claim that the change would have the same result everywhere.

questions.prompt: What does "convenient" mean in the third paragraph?
options: More fashionable than other choices.
Approved only by newspaper editors.
Available only to a small group.
Easy to use in everyday circumstances.
questions.explanation: 借杯、还杯指引和接受自带杯的说明，都使选择可重复使用杯子更容易实行，因此 convenient 表示方便。
questions.quote: The idea was to make the reusable choice more convenient during an ordinary busy day.

reading.title: 推荐列表之外
reading.subtitle: Beyond the Familiar Recommendation
reading.body:
When Daniel moved to a new city, he used a local activity app to choose places to visit. After he saved two photography exhibitions, the app began recommending more exhibitions with similar descriptions. At first, he welcomed the suggestions. They reduced the effort of searching through unfamiliar listings, and several led him to events he enjoyed.

Over time, however, his list became less varied. He rarely saw public lectures, walking groups, or small theatre performances, even though he might have liked them. The app was responding to his previous choices, but those choices represented only a small part of his interests. A convenient starting point was becoming a narrow picture of what he wanted.

Daniel raised the issue in a user workshop. The developers explained that they could not show every available event equally on the opening screen. They nevertheless agreed that people should have more control over the balance between familiar and unfamiliar suggestions. A later version included a discovery setting. Users could choose how often they wanted to see activities outside their usual categories.

The app also became more transparent about its recommendations. A short note explained whether an event appeared because of a saved interest, a nearby location, or a user's request to explore. These explanations did not make every suggestion useful. They did, however, give users a way to interpret the list and change it. Daniel continued using the app, but he also checked the full event calendar occasionally. For him, good recommendations were helpful guides to a city, not a complete account of everything the city could offer.

questions.prompt: What does the passage suggest about recommendation systems?
options: They should offer no personalised suggestions.
They always understand a person's complete interests.
They make full event calendars unnecessary.
They are more useful when people can understand and adjust them.
questions.explanation: 后半部分围绕调节发现比例、解释推荐依据展开，强调用户理解和控制推荐结果的能力。
questions.quote: They did, however, give users a way to interpret the list and change it.

questions.prompt: What did the discovery setting allow users to choose?
options: How much to charge for each event.
How often to receive suggestions outside their usual categories.
Which events should be removed from the city's calendar.
How many photographs an exhibition should contain.
questions.explanation: discovery setting 让用户选择看到平时类别以外活动的频率。
questions.quote: Users could choose how often they wanted to see activities outside their usual categories.

questions.prompt: Why did Daniel still check the full event calendar?
options: He wanted to avoid missing possibilities beyond the suggested list.
He had stopped enjoying photography exhibitions altogether.
The developers had removed all personalised recommendations.
He believed the app never provided useful suggestions.
questions.explanation: 他把推荐看作有帮助的引导，而非城市所有活动的完整清单，因此仍查看完整日历以发现其他可能。
questions.quote: For him, good recommendations were helpful guides to a city, not a complete account of everything the city could offer.

questions.prompt: What does "transparent" mean in the fourth paragraph?
options: Showing events only on a clear glass screen.
Keeping the reason for a suggestion private.
Making the reasons for recommendations easier to understand.
Removing every unfamiliar activity from the list.
questions.explanation: 后一句解释每项活动出现的原因，因此 transparent 指推荐机制的说明更清楚，而非物理上的透明。
questions.quote: A short note explained whether an event appeared because of a saved interest, a nearby location, or a user's request to explore.

reading.title: 旧车站的新用途
reading.subtitle: A Shared Place with Several Purposes
reading.body:
An old station building in a small town had stood empty for years. When the council invited suggestions for its future, residents proposed a reading room, a rehearsal space, and a place for local makers to sell their work. The building was too small to provide separate rooms for every activity. Choosing a single purpose would have been simple, but it would also have excluded many of the people who wanted to use it.

A volunteer group suggested a temporary programme before any permanent changes were made. For three months, quiet activities would take place on weekday mornings, rehearsals on two evenings, and a small market on Saturdays. Folding furniture could be moved easily, and equipment would be stored in a shared cupboard. A notice at the entrance explained the weekly schedule.

The trial soon revealed problems that had been missed in the original proposals. Some neighbours found evening noise disturbing. Market organisers needed more time to clear the tables, and readers sometimes arrived without checking the schedule. The group responded by ending rehearsals earlier, leaving longer gaps between activities, and posting updates in several nearby shops as well as online.

At the end of the trial, the council had more than a collection of preferences. It had observations about how different uses worked in practice. The final plan still involved compromise, but residents could discuss concrete examples instead of imagining only their ideal version of the building. The old station became a shared place through repeated adjustments. Its success depended less on finding one perfect use than on creating a workable way for different users to share limited space.

questions.prompt: What was most important in making the old station a shared place?
options: Selecting only the quietest activity.
Allowing every group to use it at any time.
Testing and adjusting how different uses could fit together.
Dividing it into many new permanent rooms immediately.
questions.explanation: 全文说明临时试行揭示了实际问题，再通过调整时间和信息通知形成可行共享方式。
questions.quote: The old station became a shared place through repeated adjustments.

questions.prompt: What did the group do about complaints concerning evening noise?
options: It moved the market to weekday mornings.
It stopped publishing the schedule.
It asked readers to bring their own furniture.
It arranged for rehearsals to finish earlier.
questions.explanation: 面对晚间噪声等问题，志愿组采取的措施之一是让排练更早结束。
questions.quote: The group responded by ending rehearsals earlier, leaving longer gaps between activities, and posting updates in several nearby shops as well as online.

questions.prompt: Why was the trial useful to the council?
options: It proved that residents had exactly the same preferences.
It provided practical evidence for discussing the final plan.
It removed the need for any compromise.
It showed that the building had to remain empty.
questions.explanation: 试行带来了不同活动在实际运行中的观察材料，使居民能够讨论具体例子，而不仅是各自想象中的方案。
questions.quote: It had observations about how different uses worked in practice.

questions.prompt: What does "temporary" mean in the second paragraph?
options: Intended to last for a limited period.
Designed to continue without any review.
Available only to council employees.
Too expensive for local residents.
questions.explanation: 该方案为期三个月，并且在永久改动前试行，所以 temporary 表示有时间限制的、临时的。
questions.quote: A volunteer group suggested a temporary programme before any permanent changes were made.

reading.title: 平均时间不够说明问题
reading.subtitle: Why the Average Was Not Enough
reading.body:
Leah was choosing between two routes to a weekly course across town. A travel website showed that Route A took an average of thirty minutes, while Route B took thirty-five. Since she wanted to spend less time travelling, Route A seemed the obvious choice. Yet after several weeks, she noticed that her journeys on it were difficult to plan around.

Some trips on Route A took only twenty minutes. On other evenings, traffic and a missed connection made the same journey last nearly an hour. Route B required a longer walk, but its journey times were more consistent. Leah began keeping a simple record of her departure and arrival times, along with notes about unusual delays. She did not expect this small record to describe every possible journey; she wanted information relevant to her own schedule.

The record changed the question she asked. Instead of asking only which route was faster on average, she asked which one was more likely to get her to class before it began. For this purpose, a slightly longer but more predictable journey was easier to manage. When she travelled on a free afternoon without a fixed appointment, she sometimes chose Route A instead.

The website's average had not necessarily been wrong. It had simply left out a feature that mattered to her decision: the variation between trips. Leah learned that a number can be accurate and still be incomplete for a particular task. Understanding a useful figure therefore involves asking how it was produced, what it leaves out, and whether those missing details affect the choice one needs to make.

questions.prompt: What is the main lesson Leah learned?
options: Travel websites always report incorrect figures.
A useful decision may require information beyond an average.
The route with the shortest walk is always best.
Personal records can describe every possible journey.
questions.explanation: 文章强调平均数可能准确，但未包含对决策重要的行程波动，因而还需要理解数字省略了什么。
questions.quote: Leah learned that a number can be accurate and still be incomplete for a particular task.

questions.prompt: According to the website, what was the average journey time for Route B?
options: Twenty minutes.
Thirty minutes.
Nearly an hour.
Thirty-five minutes.
questions.explanation: 首段给出的 Route B 平均用时是 thirty-five minutes，即 35 分钟。
questions.quote: A travel website showed that Route A took an average of thirty minutes, while Route B took thirty-five.

questions.prompt: Why did Leah sometimes still choose Route A on a free afternoon?
options: Arriving by a fixed time was less important on those trips.
Route A had become completely free of delays.
