The website no longer showed Route B.
She had stopped caring about travel time in every situation.
questions.explanation: 没有固定约定的下午，对准时到达的要求较低，所以她仍可能选择平均较快但波动较大的路线。
questions.quote: When she travelled on a free afternoon without a fixed appointment, she sometimes chose Route A instead.

questions.prompt: What does "consistent" mean when describing Route B's journey times?
options: Always shorter than twenty minutes.
Impossible to record.
Relatively steady from one trip to another.
Dependent only on the price of a ticket.
questions.explanation: 前文说 Route A 用时变化很大，Route B 与之对比，consistent 指各次行程用时相对稳定。
questions.quote: Route B required a longer walk, but its journey times were more consistent.

reading.title: 明信片背后的另一段历史
reading.subtitle: The Message on the Other Side
reading.body:
When Nora helped her grandfather sort a box of old postcards, she expected to find pictures of famous buildings. Many cards did show impressive streets and hotels, but the messages on the back interested her more. One described waiting for work outside a factory. Another mentioned sharing a small room with three cousins. These details were missing from the bright pictures.

For a college history project, Nora compared the cards with a travel booklet printed in the same period. The booklet presented the town as a comfortable holiday destination. Her grandfather explained that visitors and workers could experience the same place very differently. However, he warned her against treating every postcard message as a complete account. Writers often left out problems because they did not want relatives to worry.

Nora organised her display around pairs of sources. Beside a picture of a busy station, she placed a message about a cancelled journey. Each label identified what a source could show and what remained uncertain. When a date was unclear, she wrote a question rather than inventing an answer. She also covered private addresses before showing the cards to classmates.

Several visitors said the display had changed how they looked at familiar streets. Nora was pleased, although she did not describe her family's experience as the history of the whole town. The collection offered one small window into the past. Looking through it carefully meant paying attention to both the public image and the private message, while remembering that neither could reveal everything.

questions.prompt: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Private messages are more accurate than every published source.
Using different sources carefully can enrich our view of the past.
Travel booklets should be replaced by family collections.
A town's history can be explained through its station alone.
questions.explanation: 文章比较宣传册、图像和私人文字，既展示它们互补的价值，也提醒读者注意每种资料的局限。
questions.quote: Looking through it carefully meant paying attention to both the public image and the private message, while remembering that neither could reveal everything.

questions.prompt: What did Nora do when a postcard's date was unclear?
options: She borrowed a date from the travel booklet.
She removed the postcard from the project.
She asked visitors to vote on the date.
She marked the uncertainty with a question.
questions.explanation: 面对无法确定的日期，诺拉没有自行补上答案，而是在展签上用疑问明确保留不确定性。
questions.quote: When a date was unclear, she wrote a question rather than inventing an answer.

questions.prompt: What can be inferred about cheerful messages sent to relatives?
options: They may conceal difficulties that the writer actually faced.
They were usually copied from official travel booklets.
They show that workers and tourists had identical experiences.
They contain less personal information than the pictures.
questions.explanation: 祖父说写信人可能为避免家人担心而省略问题，因此愉快的留言不能证明生活中没有困难。
questions.quote: Writers often left out problems because they did not want relatives to worry.

questions.prompt: What does "account" mean in the second paragraph?
options: A place to keep money.
A list of travel expenses.
A description of events or experiences.
A private address on a postcard.
questions.explanation: 上下文讨论明信片文字是否完整描述过去的生活经历，所以 account 在此表示记述，而不是银行账户。
questions.quote: However, he warned her against treating every postcard message as a complete account.

reading.title: 替补演员的笔记本
reading.subtitle: Ready for a Role She Might Never Play
reading.body:
At the first meeting of a college theatre production, Elena learned that she would be the understudy for the main character. She would attend rehearsals and learn the role, but another student would normally perform it. Elena smiled when the director spoke to her, then wondered privately whether she had received a task with very little purpose.

During the following week, she copied the main actor's movements into a notebook. The director noticed and suggested that she also record the reasons behind them. Why did the character turn away during an argument? What did a pause suggest? If Elena understood those choices, she could respond naturally when another performer changed their timing. Simply copying a position on the stage would not be enough.

Halfway through rehearsals, the main actor had to leave town for a family event. Elena stepped in for two afternoons. She knew the words, but she initially struggled when a chair was placed differently. Her notes about the character's intentions helped her adjust. The scene continued without anyone needing to stop and explain each movement again. Afterwards, she added several new observations to her notebook.

The main actor returned before the public performance, so Elena never played the role for an audience. Nevertheless, the director thanked her for keeping rehearsals moving. Elena also found that she understood the whole play more clearly than before. She had learned to prepare for responsibility without knowing whether she would receive public attention. Her contribution had become visible to her, even if it remained invisible to most people buying tickets.

questions.prompt: What does Elena learn through being an understudy?
options: A performance can succeed without regular rehearsals.
The best actors copy every movement exactly.
Preparation can be valuable even without public recognition.
Supporting roles should be avoided by ambitious students.
questions.explanation: 埃琳娜虽未正式登台，却帮助排练顺利推进并理解了整部戏，认识到准备和幕后贡献同样有价值。
questions.quote: She had learned to prepare for responsibility without knowing whether she would receive public attention.

questions.prompt: Why did the main actor miss two afternoons of rehearsals?
options: The actor left town for a family event.
The actor was attending another theatre audition.
The director wanted Elena to perform publicly.
The theatre was being prepared for ticket sales.
questions.explanation: 原文明确说明主角演员因家庭活动需要离城，因此埃琳娜临时代演了两个下午。
questions.quote: Halfway through rehearsals, the main actor had to leave town for a family event.

questions.prompt: Why did understanding the character help Elena when the chair moved?
options: It allowed her to ignore the other actors' words.
It meant the director no longer needed a script.
It helped her persuade the main actor to leave.
It gave her a basis for adapting instead of repeating positions.
questions.explanation: 椅子位置变化使机械模仿失效，而人物意图能指导新的动作，因此理解动机有助于应对舞台变化。
questions.quote: Her notes about the character's intentions helped her adjust.

questions.prompt: What is an "understudy" in this passage?
options: A person responsible for selling theatre tickets.
An actor prepared to replace another performer when needed.
A writer who checks the final version of a script.
A visitor who watches the first rehearsal.
questions.explanation: 首段说明她学习同一角色但通常由另一名学生演出，后来又临时代演，可知该词指替补演员。
questions.quote: She would attend rehearsals and learn the role, but another student would normally perform it.

reading.title: 没有拍到的那个夜晚
reading.subtitle: An Evening Under Uncooperative Skies
reading.body:
The astronomy society advertised an evening of observing a distant planet from a field outside town. Sam borrowed a camera and imagined returning with a sharp image that he could post online. When the group arrived, however, thin clouds covered much of the sky. Through the telescope, the planet appeared only briefly before fading from view again.

Some beginners suggested increasing the camera's settings until something brighter appeared on the screen. The group leader explained that a brighter picture would not necessarily contain more useful detail. She asked everyone to make a simple observation record instead. They noted the time, the cloud cover, and what they could actually distinguish. A drawing with two clear features was more useful than a confident description of five uncertain ones.

During a break, the leader showed photographs from earlier sessions. Beside the successful images were pages describing nights when equipment had failed or clouds had arrived unexpectedly. Sam was surprised that these pages had been kept. The leader said they helped the society plan future visits and compare results fairly. Without the conditions, a picture could give a misleading impression of what had been easy to observe.

By the end of the evening, Sam had no photograph worth displaying. He did have a page of notes and a small drawing completed during one clear moment. Later, he placed them beside the image he had originally hoped to make. The gap no longer seemed simply disappointing. It reminded him that observing involves deciding what the available view supports, rather than filling the darkness with what one wishes to see.

questions.prompt: What is the main lesson of Sam's evening?
options: Bright camera settings always create scientific detail.
Unsuccessful observing sessions should be forgotten.
A drawing is always more accurate than a photograph.
Careful observation includes recording limits and conditions.
questions.explanation: 全文通过云层、记录和失败夜晚的档案说明，科学观察需要忠于实际所见并记录条件与限制。
questions.quote: It reminded him that observing involves deciding what the available view supports, rather than filling the darkness with what one wishes to see.

questions.prompt: What did the leader ask the beginners to record?
options: Only the camera settings used for successful pictures.
The time, cloud cover, and details they could distinguish.
The names of everyone who had borrowed equipment.
The number of photographs they planned to post online.
questions.explanation: 领队要求记录时间、云层情况和确实能够辨认的细节，帮助大家区分观察结果与想象。
questions.quote: They noted the time, the cloud cover, and what they could actually distinguish.

questions.prompt: Why might a successful photograph alone give an incomplete impression?
options: Its colours would prove that the telescope was damaged.
It would show every difficulty described in the notes.
It could hide the conditions and unsuccessful attempts behind it.
It would prevent the group from planning another visit.
questions.explanation: 领队保留失败记录以便比较和安排活动，可推知单张成功照片可能掩盖取得结果时的条件与困难。
questions.quote: Without the conditions, a picture could give a misleading impression of what had been easy to observe.

questions.prompt: What does "distinguish" mean in the second paragraph?
options: Recognise clearly enough to tell what something is.
Change the brightness of a camera screen.
Imagine features that a picture might contain.
Explain why clouds arrive at a particular time.
questions.explanation: 后文以两项清楚特征和五项不确定描述作对比，因此 distinguish 指实际能够辨认出来。
questions.quote: A drawing with two clear features was more useful than a confident description of five uncertain ones.

reading.title: 食谱上的空白
reading.subtitle: What the Recipe Did Not Say
reading.body:
When Luis moved away to college, his aunt gave him a handwritten recipe for the vegetable soup served at family gatherings. He followed the list carefully, measuring each ingredient and checking the cooking time. The soup was pleasant, but it did not taste quite like the one he remembered. He assumed that he had made a mistake.

During a video call, his aunt asked what vegetables he had bought. Luis held up the recipe, which simply said to use two bowls of mixed vegetables. She laughed and explained that the mixture changed with the season and with whatever was available in the market. The written page recorded a starting point, not every decision she made while cooking. She had never thought to write down those decisions.

Luis began asking about the choices behind the instructions. His aunt described how she compared the size of the pieces and adjusted the amount of liquid. He added these explanations in the margins. He also wrote down a change of his own: a local vegetable that was easy to find near his college. His aunt asked him to describe its taste next time rather than dismissing it as an incorrect ingredient.

At the next family gathering, Luis brought his version of the soup and the expanded recipe. Some relatives preferred the familiar mixture; others wanted to try his addition again. No one suggested throwing away the old page. Instead, they made copies with space for further notes. Luis began to see a family recipe as a conversation across kitchens, carrying remembered choices while leaving room for new ones.

questions.prompt: What does the passage suggest about family recipes?
options: They can preserve tradition while developing through explanation and adaptation.
They should contain exact rules for every possible ingredient.
They become less valuable whenever a new cook adds notes.
They are useful only when cooked in the original kitchen.
questions.explanation: 路易斯通过询问补充隐含经验，并加入当地食材，说明家传食谱可在传承中继续解释和发展。
questions.quote: Luis began to see a family recipe as a conversation across kitchens, carrying remembered choices while leaving room for new ones.

questions.prompt: Where did Luis add his aunt's explanations?
options: On labels attached to the vegetables.
In a message sent to every relative.
In the margins of the recipe.
On the college kitchen's noticeboard.
questions.explanation: 第三段直接说明路易斯把阿姨对烹调选择的解释写在食谱页边的空白处。
questions.quote: He added these explanations in the margins.

questions.prompt: What does the aunt's response to the local vegetable suggest?
options: She believed that family dishes should never leave home.
She valued thoughtful experimentation within the tradition.
She expected Luis to replace all the original vegetables.
She wanted relatives to stop using written recipes.
questions.explanation: 阿姨愿意听新食材的味道而不直接认定错误，表明她接纳有思考的尝试，并非要求完全抛弃传统。
questions.quote: His aunt asked him to describe its taste next time rather than dismissing it as an incorrect ingredient.

questions.prompt: What does "expanded" mean in "the expanded recipe"?
options: Printed in much larger letters.
Prepared for a larger family gathering.
Changed into a different language.
Made fuller by adding information.
questions.explanation: 路易斯加入阿姨的说明和自己的改动，因而 expanded 指内容得到补充扩展，而非字体或份量变大。
questions.quote: At the next family gathering, Luis brought his version of the soup and the expanded recipe.

reading.title: 接力区里的那几步
reading.subtitle: The Race Between the Runners
reading.body:
Before the college relay festival, the four members of Oak House's team spent most of their practice time running separately. Each wanted a faster personal time. During their first practice race together, however, they lost ground whenever the baton changed hands. One runner slowed too early, while another reached backwards before the baton was close enough.

Their captain, Priya, asked a volunteer coach to watch one session. He timed the exchanges rather than the full race. Then he showed the runners where they hesitated. The problem was not a lack of effort. Each person was guessing what the next runner would do. The coach suggested practising a simple signal and agreeing on a comfortable starting point for each pair.

At first, this work felt less exciting than racing around the track. They repeated short exchanges and stopped often to compare what each runner had noticed. When one pair tried to copy another pair's starting point, their timing became worse. Priya realised that a shared method did not require identical distances. Different running styles meant that the details needed to be adjusted together.

On festival day, Oak House finished behind two stronger teams. Nevertheless, all four exchanges were smooth, and the runners were satisfied with the improvement they could identify. Their final position did not erase the value of the practice. Priya kept the exchange notes for the next team captain, including the reasons for each pair's decisions. The team had discovered that a relay depends on what happens between individual performances as well as on how fast each person can run.

questions.prompt: What is the main message of the passage?
options: A relay team's final position is its only useful measure.
Team performance depends partly on carefully coordinated transitions.
Every runner should use exactly the same starting distance.
Individual speed has no role in a successful relay.
questions.explanation: 个人跑得快并未解决交棒损失，队员通过协调信号和起跑点改进衔接，说明团队成绩也依赖成员之间的配合。
questions.quote: The team had discovered that a relay depends on what happens between individual performances as well as on how fast each person can run.

questions.prompt: What did the volunteer coach time at the session?
options: Only Priya's fastest lap.
The journey to the festival track.
The runners' rest periods.
The changes of baton between runners.
questions.explanation: 教练把观察重点放在交棒过程，并为此计时，而不是只记录整场比赛或个人圈速。
questions.quote: He timed the exchanges rather than the full race.

questions.prompt: Why did Priya include reasons in the notes for the next captain?
options: The next team would need to adapt the method to its own runners.
The notes would prove that running practice was unnecessary.
The same distances were certain to suit every future team.
The festival organisers required a written race report.
questions.explanation: 文章已显示不同组合不能机械照搬起跑点，保留原因便于后来队伍理解原则，再按自身情况调整。
questions.quote: Different running styles meant that the details needed to be adjusted together.

questions.prompt: What does "identical" mean in the third paragraph?
options: Chosen by a team captain.
Suitable for a long race.
Exactly the same.
Difficult to measure.
questions.explanation: 不同跑法需要调整具体距离，所以 identical 在这里指各组使用完全相同的数值。
questions.quote: Priya realised that a shared method did not require identical distances.

reading.title: 盒子越厚越好吗
reading.subtitle: A Box Designed for Its Journey
reading.body:
A small ceramics studio asked a design class to improve the boxes used for sending cups to customers. The owner had responded to broken handles by adding more layers of paper around every cup. The packages grew larger, but some cups still arrived damaged. The class began by examining how the objects moved inside their boxes.

Using wooden models in place of real cups, students tried several arrangements. They noticed that thick paper could become loose during repeated movement. A model could then slide towards the side of the box, leaving its handle exposed. Adding another outside layer did little to prevent this movement. The class therefore designed a folded insert that held the body of the cup in position without pressing on the handle.

The first insert was difficult to assemble. Studio workers had to stop and study a diagram for each fold, which interrupted their usual packing routine. The students simplified the shape and marked the upper side clearly. They also tested whether someone who had not seen the design could put it together using the printed instructions. This revealed one final fold that needed a clearer label.

The owner agreed to try the revised package on a small group of orders and keep a record of the results. The students did not promise that damage would disappear completely. Their proposal connected the form of the package to the conditions of its journey and the work of the people packing it. They had learned that protection could depend more on controlling movement than on surrounding an object with ever more material.

questions.prompt: What is the main point of the packaging project?
options: Customers should accept broken handles as unavoidable.
The largest package always offers the greatest protection.
Effective packaging should address movement and practical assembly.
Printed instructions can replace every physical design test.
questions.explanation: 学生先控制杯子在盒内的移动，再改进工人组装的便利性，说明保护效果与实际使用过程需要一起考虑。
questions.quote: Their proposal connected the form of the package to the conditions of its journey and the work of the people packing it.

questions.prompt: What did students use instead of real cups during the early tests?
options: Wooden models.
Empty paper envelopes.
Broken ceramic handles.
Customers' returned orders.
questions.explanation: 为观察不同包装中的移动情况，学生在早期试验中使用木制模型替代真正的陶瓷杯。
questions.quote: Using wooden models in place of real cups, students tried several arrangements.

questions.prompt: Why did students ask an unfamiliar person to assemble the insert?
options: They wanted to remove the need for written instructions.
They expected that person to redesign the cup handle.
They needed someone to inspect customers' old orders.
They wanted to see whether the design made sense without prior knowledge.
questions.explanation: 陌生使用者没有参与设计，可帮助发现设计者因熟悉流程而忽略的说明问题，文中因此找出了需改进的折叠标记。
questions.quote: They also tested whether someone who had not seen the design could put it together using the printed instructions.

questions.prompt: What does "exposed" mean when describing the handle?
options: Clearly painted in a bright colour.
Left without adequate protection.
Already attached to the wooden model.
Hidden beneath several outer layers.
questions.explanation: 模型滑向盒边后杯柄失去缓冲保护，因此 exposed 在此指暴露而缺少足够保护。
questions.quote: A model could then slide towards the side of the box, leaving its handle exposed.

reading.title: 鸟少了，还是听不见了
reading.subtitle: Listening for the Birds Again
reading.body:
A group of students regularly counted birds beside a stream near their college. On their first visits, they heard calls from several kinds of birds among the trees. After construction began on a nearby road, their records showed fewer birds. Some members wanted to announce that the building work had driven the birds away.

Their tutor asked them to look more closely at how they had collected the information. Most birds had been identified by sound rather than sight. Heavy machines now made it harder to hear quiet calls. This did not prove that the birds were still present, but it meant that a lower count could have more than one explanation. The students needed a way to separate a possible change in wildlife from a change in their ability to notice it.

They arranged visits before the machines started in the morning and kept their usual afternoon sessions. They also recorded how much noise they heard at each visit. Morning observations revealed some birds that were rarely recorded later in the day. However, the students knew that birds might behave differently at different hours, even without construction. They included this difficulty in their report.

The final display presented the observations without claiming to settle every question about the stream. It explained why matching methods mattered and proposed continuing the work after the road was finished. Several members had initially worried that discussing uncertainty would weaken their message. They eventually decided that showing how a conclusion had been tested made their concern for the stream more credible.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of the passage?
options: To show that construction never affects wildlife.
To argue that bird calls are unsuitable for any research.
To prove that morning counts reveal the complete bird population.
To show why changes in observation conditions need careful consideration.
questions.explanation: 施工噪声可能影响听见鸟鸣的能力，学生据此调整记录并说明局限，重点是区分观察条件变化和对象变化。
questions.quote: The students needed a way to separate a possible change in wildlife from a change in their ability to notice it.

questions.prompt: How had most birds been identified on the students' early visits?
options: By the shape of their nests.
By the sounds they made.
By photographs from the road workers.
By marks placed on their wings.
questions.explanation: 原文指出早期大部分鸟类通过声音而非外形识别，这也是施工噪声会影响计数的原因。
questions.quote: Most birds had been identified by sound rather than sight.

questions.prompt: Why could morning and afternoon counts not settle the issue by themselves?
options: The construction machines operated all night without stopping.
The students had decided not to listen for bird calls.
The birds' daily routines could also influence the differences.
The tutor believed that every count was equally accurate.
questions.explanation: 学生认识到不同时间鸟类活动本就可能不同，因此早晚差异不能完全归因于施工噪声的变化。
questions.quote: However, the students knew that birds might behave differently at different hours, even without construction.

questions.prompt: What does "credible" mean in the last paragraph?
options: Believable because it deserves trust.
Urgent enough to stop every activity.
Simple enough to finish without records.
Popular with everyone who reads it.
questions.explanation: 他们通过展示检验过程而增强结论的可信程度，所以 credible 指值得相信，而非受所有人欢迎。
questions.quote: They eventually decided that showing how a conclusion had been tested made their concern for the stream more credible.

reading.title: 把笑点翻译过去
reading.subtitle: Finding the Joke in Another Language
reading.body:
For a student magazine, Amira translated a short comic story written by a visiting author. She found dictionary meanings for every unfamiliar word and carefully preserved the order of the sentences. Yet when a friend read her translation, he understood the events without finding them funny. The sentences were correct, but the joke seemed to have disappeared.

Amira returned to the original story. Its central joke depended on a phrase that could refer both to a food dish and to an embarrassing mistake. In her language, those meanings belonged to completely different expressions. Explaining both meanings in a long note would help readers understand the wordplay, but it would also interrupt the moment when they were supposed to laugh.

She prepared two versions for a small reading group. One kept the original phrase and added a short note. The other used a different joke that fitted the same character and situation. Readers could follow the second version more easily, although one felt that it sounded too modern for the setting. Amira revised the language and discussed the change with the author before choosing it for publication.

In a brief introduction, she described the choice she had made. She did not claim that every joke should be changed or that notes were always a mistake. A poem, a historical letter, or a language textbook might call for a different decision. For this comic story, she wanted readers to experience the character's awkward moment at roughly the same point. Translation, she discovered, involved deciding which effects mattered most, as well as understanding what individual words meant.

questions.prompt: What does Amira discover about translation?
options: Translators may need to consider a text's effects as well as its words.
Correct dictionary meanings always preserve a story's humour.
Explanatory notes should be removed from every kind of text.
Authors should avoid jokes that involve more than one meaning.
questions.explanation: 阿米拉先发现逐词正确仍会丢失笑点，再比较不同方案，认识到翻译还需考虑文本希望产生的效果。
questions.quote: Translation, she discovered, involved deciding which effects mattered most, as well as understanding what individual words meant.

questions.prompt: What problem did one reader find in the version with a different joke?
options: It explained the wordplay in a note that was too long.
It changed the main character into the story's author.
It sounded too modern for the story's setting.
It repeated the same unfamiliar word several times.
questions.explanation: 采用新笑话的版本更容易理解，但一位读者认为其语言相对故事背景过于现代，因此她继续修改。
questions.quote: Readers could follow the second version more easily, although one felt that it sounded too modern for the setting.

questions.prompt: Why does the passage mention a poem, a historical letter, and a textbook?
options: To identify the texts that Amira planned to translate next.
To suggest that a suitable translation choice depends on the purpose of the text.
To show that humour appears equally often in every kind of writing.
To explain why the author rejected the final magazine version.
questions.explanation: 这些文本被用来说明其他类型可能需要不同决定，可推知阿米拉并不把自己的喜剧翻译方案视为通用规则。
questions.quote: A poem, a historical letter, or a language textbook might call for a different decision.

questions.prompt: What does "awkward" mean when describing the character's moment?
options: Unusually dangerous.
Carefully planned.
Extremely private.
Embarrassing or uncomfortable.
questions.explanation: 前文解释笑点涉及令人难堪的错误，结尾的 awkward moment 正是对应人物尴尬不自在的处境。
questions.quote: Its central joke depended on a phrase that could refer both to a food dish and to an embarrassing mistake.

reading.title: 合奏中学会听见别人
reading.subtitle: Learning to Leave Space in the Music
reading.body:
Theo was pleased when he was invited to join a student music group as its second guitarist. He practised his part until he could play every note without looking at the page. At the first rehearsal, however, the singer asked him to play less during the opening verse. Theo wondered why accuracy was not enough.

The group recorded a short section and listened to it together. Theo could hear that his busy guitar part covered the ends of the singer's lines. The keyboard player was also filling many of the same spaces. Neither player had made an obvious mistake while practising alone. The difficulty appeared only when their correct parts were combined. They needed to decide how the different sounds would fit.

For the next rehearsal, the group marked places where one instrument would step back. Theo played a simpler pattern during the verse and saved his fuller part for the final section. The keyboard player left a pause after certain vocal lines. These changes made the contrast clearer without requiring anyone to play louder. Theo began listening for the singer's breathing as well as counting his own beats.

At their small concert, Theo played fewer notes than he had originally prepared. He nevertheless felt more involved in the performance because he could hear how his choices affected everyone else. After the concert, he kept both versions of the guitar part. The first showed what he could play by himself; the second showed what the song needed from him. He had learned that musical contribution sometimes takes the form of leaving a space.

questions.prompt: What does Theo learn about playing in a group?
options: Solo practice usually prevents musicians from improving.
An effective contribution may involve simplifying one's own part.
The strongest musician should always play the loudest.
A second guitarist should perform exactly like the keyboard player.
questions.explanation: 西奥通过减少主歌中的音符为歌声留出空间，认识到合奏贡献取决于整体效果，未必是演奏更多。
questions.quote: He had learned that musical contribution sometimes takes the form of leaving a space.

questions.prompt: When did Theo decide to use his fuller guitar part?
options: While the singer was taking a breath in every line.
Only during individual practice before the concert.
Throughout the entire opening verse.
In the final section of the song.
questions.explanation: 新编排把主歌改为简洁的节奏型，将较丰富的吉他段落保留到歌曲最后部分，以形成层次。
questions.quote: Theo played a simpler pattern during the verse and saved his fuller part for the final section.

questions.prompt: Why was the recording useful even though the musicians knew their own parts?
options: It revealed an overall effect that individual practice had not exposed.
It allowed them to avoid attending any more group rehearsals.
It proved that the written music contained incorrect notes.
It showed that the singer needed to perform without instruments.
questions.explanation: 每个人独自练习时并无明显错误，录音却显示声音相互遮盖，因此它帮助成员听见独奏无法呈现的整体问题。
questions.quote: The difficulty appeared only when their correct parts were combined.

questions.prompt: What does "contrast" mean in the third paragraph?
options: The exact number of written notes.
A mistake caused by playing too quietly.
A noticeable difference between sections.
An agreement to use the same instrument.
questions.explanation: 主歌较简洁而结尾较丰满，使不同段落的听感区别更清楚，因此 contrast 在此指段落之间的反差。
questions.quote: These changes made the contrast clearer without requiring anyone to play louder.

reading.title: 杯沿上的一点不圆
reading.subtitle: The Useful Imperfection
reading.body:
In her first pottery class, Mei tried to make a bowl with a perfectly circular rim. Whenever one side looked higher, she pressed it down. The other side then seemed uneven, and she adjusted that too. By the time she stopped, the clay wall had become thin and the bowl no longer held its shape.

Her teacher placed two finished bowls on the table. One had a regular outline and the other had a slightly uneven edge. She asked Mei to hold them and imagine using each one. Mei preferred the second because a shallow curve fitted comfortably beneath her thumb. The teacher explained that an irregular shape could be accidental, but it could also be a deliberate response to how an object would be held.

This did not mean that every mistake should be praised. For her next attempt, Mei first checked whether the base was stable and whether the walls were strong enough. Then she shaped a small curve in the rim and left the rest alone. She drew the intended shape before returning the bowl to the shelf, so she could compare it with the result after drying and firing.

At the class exhibition, visitors noticed the curve and asked about it. Mei described both her failed first bowl and the choices behind the second. She no longer measured improvement only by how closely a piece resembled a perfect circle. The class had helped her distinguish between an unwanted weakness and a useful variation. Making something by hand involved learning when to correct the material and when a careful decision had already done enough.

questions.prompt: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Every irregular shape should be accepted as a successful design.
Pottery skill can be measured only through perfect circles.
Craft skill includes judging which differences are useful and intentional.
A comfortable bowl can be made without checking its strength.
questions.explanation: 老师既肯定适合持握的曲线，也要求检查稳固与强度，说明手艺进步包括辨别有用变化和真正缺陷。
questions.quote: The class had helped her distinguish between an unwanted weakness and a useful variation.

questions.prompt: Why did Mei prefer holding the bowl with the uneven edge?
options: A shallow curve rested comfortably beneath her thumb.
Its walls were thinner than those of her first bowl.
Its decoration matched the drawing in her notebook.
Its circular outline was easier to copy.
questions.explanation: 文中明确写到第二只碗的浅弧线适合拇指放置，舒适的持握感是她偏好它的直接原因。
questions.quote: Mei preferred the second because a shallow curve fitted comfortably beneath her thumb.

questions.prompt: What does Mei's drawing before drying and firing suggest?
options: She expected the bowl to become perfectly circular by itself.
She wanted visitors to judge only the decoration.
She believed that structural checks were no longer necessary.
She wanted to compare an intended choice with the finished result.
questions.explanation: 提前画下目标形状并在烧成后比较，表明她希望检验有意设计与实际结果的关系，而非事后为变化找理由。
questions.quote: She drew the intended shape before returning the bowl to the shelf, so she could compare it with the result after drying and firing.

questions.prompt: What does "deliberate" mean in the second paragraph?
options: Produced without any attention.
Made intentionally after consideration.
Likely to disappear during use.
Too difficult for beginners to notice.
questions.explanation: 原文将 accidental 与 deliberate 对照，后者指为了持握体验而有意识作出的设计选择。
questions.quote: The teacher explained that an irregular shape could be accidental, but it could also be a deliberate response to how an object would be held.

reading.title: 重读结局之前
reading.subtitle: The Clues They Read Differently
reading.body:
At a college reading club, the members disagreed about the ending of a mystery novel. One group thought the main character had deceived her friends throughout the story. Another believed that she had misunderstood events herself. Each group remembered a few lines that seemed to support its view, and the discussion quickly became a contest over who had understood the book correctly.

The club leader asked everyone to return to one scene near the beginning. In it, the main character described seeing someone leave a house. At the time, readers had accepted her description without question. Later chapters revealed that the street was poorly lit and that she had only seen the person's coat. The early statement sounded much more certain than the information behind it.

Members then made two lists: events directly shown in the story and explanations offered by the character. Some items they had treated as facts moved into the second list. This did not settle the ending, but it changed the quality of the discussion. People began asking what the character could reasonably know at each point, instead of judging every early statement using information revealed much later.

By the end of the meeting, the members still preferred different interpretations. They could now explain those differences through details in the text. One student said that uncertainty no longer felt like a flaw she needed to remove before enjoying the novel. The group chose to reread another chapter the following week, interested in how a narrator could guide their attention while leaving room for them to question the guide.

questions.prompt: What is the main focus of the passage?
options: How a reading club selected its next mystery novel.
Why every mystery novel should have one clear explanation.
How a writer can avoid describing uncertain events.
How examining narrative evidence improved a discussion without ending disagreement.
questions.explanation: 读书会区分直接呈现的事件与人物解释后，仍保有分歧，却能以具体文本依据展开更有质量的讨论。
questions.quote: This did not settle the ending, but it changed the quality of the discussion.

questions.prompt: What had the main character actually seen outside the house?
options: The person's face under a bright lamp.
Only the person's coat.
A written message left at the door.
Two friends entering the same street.
questions.explanation: 后文揭示街道光线不足，人物实际上仅看到了对方的外套，因此早先的确定描述值得重新审视。
questions.quote: Later chapters revealed that the street was poorly lit and that she had only seen the person's coat.

questions.prompt: Why was it useful to ask what the character knew at each point?
options: It proved that every remembered line was false.
It allowed members to ignore the later chapters completely.
It helped separate the character's limited view from the reader's later knowledge.
It established that the narrator had planned every event in advance.
questions.explanation: 读者读到后面后掌握了新信息，回到人物当时的知识范围，有助于避免用事后知识简单判断她的早期陈述。
questions.quote: People began asking what the character could reasonably know at each point, instead of judging every early statement using information revealed much later.

questions.prompt: What does "flaw" mean in the last paragraph?
options: A fault or weakness.
A surprising final event.
A rule of the reading club.
A description of a setting.
questions.explanation: 学生不再觉得必须消除不确定性才能欣赏小说，因此这里的 flaw 指她原先认为需要去除的缺点或不足。
questions.quote: One student said that uncertainty no longer felt like a flaw she needed to remove before enjoying the novel.

reading.title: 机器人走到真实地面上
reading.subtitle: When the Robot Left the Screen
reading.body:
A beginner robotics team designed a small vehicle to follow a line around a course. On the computer, its program handled every turn correctly. The students therefore expected the physical robot to finish its first test without difficulty. Instead, it turned too late at one corner and stopped completely where a bright window lit the floor.

The team initially tried rewriting large sections of code. A visiting engineer suggested changing one condition at a time. They moved the course away from the window without altering the program, then tested the same corner on two surfaces. These comparisons helped them see that the light affected the line sensor, while the smoother surface allowed the wheels to slide during a turn.

They adjusted the sensor settings and reduced speed before corners. However, a slower program that worked on the smooth floor performed poorly on the rougher one. The students decided to record the surface and lighting conditions beside every test result. They also added a simple check at the start so the robot could measure the line against the surrounding floor before moving.

At the club demonstration, someone asked why the computer version had looked so successful. The students explained that their simulation had used ideal conditions and left out several features of the room. They still found it useful for trying basic ideas quickly. They simply understood its limits more clearly. Their final presentation included a failed test as well as a successful run, showing how an unexpected stop had helped them connect a tidy program with a less tidy physical world.

questions.prompt: What does the team's experience mainly show?
options: Testing in the physical world can reveal conditions missing from a simulation.
A robot program should be rewritten completely after every failure.
Computer simulations have no value for beginner engineers.
A single speed setting can work equally well on every surface.
questions.explanation: 模拟中成功的程序在真实光线和地面条件下出现问题，逐项测试帮助团队发现并补上被简化的因素。
questions.quote: They simply understood its limits more clearly.

questions.prompt: What did the bright window affect?
options: The colour printed on the computer screen.
The strength of the robot's frame.
The robot's line sensor.
The written order of the program's sections.
questions.explanation: 分别控制条件后，学生发现光照影响循线传感器，而光滑地面影响轮子的转弯表现，两者原因不同。
questions.quote: These comparisons helped them see that the light affected the line sensor, while the smoother surface allowed the wheels to slide during a turn.

questions.prompt: Why did the engineer recommend changing one condition at a time?
options: It would guarantee that every test was successful.
It would make it easier to identify what caused a change in performance.
It would remove the need to record any test results.
It would make all physical surfaces behave like the simulation.
questions.explanation: 分别改变光线和地面可让团队把表现变化与具体条件对应起来，避免同时改变多项因素后无法判断原因。
questions.quote: They moved the course away from the window without altering the program, then tested the same corner on two surfaces.

questions.prompt: What does "simulation" mean in the last paragraph?
options: A set of tools for smoothing a real floor.
A written report about the club demonstration.
A sensor that measures the surrounding light.
A computer model that imitates a real process.
questions.explanation: 前文说程序在电脑上顺利运行，结尾又讨论其理想条件，因此 simulation 指模仿真实运行的计算机模型。
questions.quote: The students explained that their simulation had used ideal conditions and left out several features of the room.

reading.title: 银幕上的脚步从哪里来
reading.subtitle: Making a Footstep Belong to a Scene
reading.body:
In a student film, a character walked through an empty railway tunnel carrying a small bag. The picture looked convincing, but the recorded footsteps were almost impossible to hear. Traffic outside had covered them during filming. The sound team invited Rina to create replacement footsteps in a quiet room, matching the actor's movements on a screen.

Rina first chose shoes like the actor's and walked over a hard board. The result sounded realistic when she listened with her eyes closed. Against the film, however, the steps felt too light. The tunnel appeared large, and the character seemed anxious. The director asked her to try a heavier rhythm and leave a slightly longer gap before the character turned around.

They recorded several versions rather than searching for one sound that would fit every scene. For a later shot outside the tunnel, the same heavy steps seemed exaggerated. A softer recording worked better there. Rina learned to compare each choice with the image and the story. A sound could be accurate to the object producing it yet unsuitable for the moment being shown.

At the screening, few viewers mentioned the footsteps. One said that the pause before the turn had made the scene feel tense. Rina took this as a useful response, even though nobody had noticed the board or the room where she worked. The finished sound directed attention towards the character rather than towards its own creation. She had helped tell the story through choices that were most effective when the audience simply accepted them as part of the film.

questions.prompt: What does Rina learn about sound work for films?
options: The audience should be able to identify every recording tool.
Sound choices should serve the scene's image and emotional effect.
Matching an actor's shoes guarantees a suitable recording.
A single realistic footstep can be reused in every setting.
questions.explanation: 同一种脚步在不同镜头中效果不同，瑞娜因此认识到声音既要配合画面，也要服务情绪和叙事。
questions.quote: Rina learned to compare each choice with the image and the story.

questions.prompt: Why were the footsteps recorded during filming difficult to hear?
options: The actor had forgotten to wear shoes.
The sound team had removed the walking scene.
The quiet recording room was too far away.
Traffic outside had covered the sound.
questions.explanation: 第一段明确交代，拍摄现场外面的交通声盖过了脚步声，因此才需要后期重新录制。
questions.quote: Traffic outside had covered them during filming.

questions.prompt: Why was the viewer's comment about tension satisfying to Rina?
options: It suggested that her choices supported the story without drawing attention to the technique.
It proved that every viewer understood how the footsteps had been recorded.
It showed that the tunnel scene no longer needed any dialogue.
It meant that the heavier recording should be used in every scene.
questions.explanation: 观众感受到转身前的紧张，却没注意录音器材和技术，说明声音自然地强化了故事所需的效果。
questions.quote: The finished sound directed attention towards the character rather than towards its own creation.

questions.prompt: What does "exaggerated" mean in the third paragraph?
options: Recorded at the wrong walking speed.
Too faint for the audience to hear.
Stronger than seemed suitable for the situation.
Completely missing from the soundtrack.
questions.explanation: 隧道中合适的沉重脚步到室外显得过强，改用较轻版本更好，因此 exaggerated 表示相对场景而言过头了。
questions.quote: For a later shot outside the tunnel, the same heavy steps seemed exaggerated.

reading.title: 一个口袋的实际考验
reading.subtitle: Putting the Pocket to Work
reading.body:
For a clothing design assignment, Jonas made a jacket with large front pockets. He thought their size would make them useful, and the jacket looked balanced when it hung on a display stand. His first tester put a notebook in one pocket and sat down. The notebook pressed against her leg, and the pocket opening became difficult to reach.

Jonas had measured the notebook while it lay flat on a table. He had not considered the way a pocket changed when a person bent or sat. His teacher suggested making a simple cloth version that could be moved around before he finished the jacket. This allowed Jonas to test several positions without cutting expensive material each time.

He invited three classmates to try the cloth pockets during ordinary tasks. One carried keys, another used a phone, and the third wanted somewhere to keep a travel card. Their comments were not identical. A position that felt natural for standing was awkward while sitting. Jonas raised the opening slightly and added a small inner section so a card would not disappear beneath larger objects.

The final jacket had pockets that looked smaller from the outside but were easier to use for the tasks he had tested. Jonas described those tasks in his presentation instead of simply calling the design practical. He also noted that three classmates could not represent every future wearer. The project changed his habit of judging clothing only from the front. A useful garment had to work with a moving person, whose daily actions were more complicated than the still pose of a display stand.

questions.prompt: What is the central idea of the passage?
options: Large pockets are always less practical than small ones.
Display stands should be removed from design classrooms.
Clothing design needs to account for real movement and use.
Testing three classmates is enough to represent every wearer.
questions.explanation: 最初静态展示中协调的口袋坐下后不好用，后续测试围绕日常动作展开，强调衣物设计要适应真实使用。
questions.quote: A useful garment had to work with a moving person, whose daily actions were more complicated than the still pose of a display stand.

questions.prompt: What did Jonas add to keep a travel card easy to find?
options: A small inner section inside the pocket.
A larger notebook attached to the jacket.
A strap connecting both pocket openings.
A transparent cover outside the jacket.
questions.explanation: 为避免卡片落到较大物品下面而难以找到，乔纳斯在口袋内部加入了一个小分区。
questions.quote: Jonas raised the opening slightly and added a small inner section so a card would not disappear beneath larger objects.

questions.prompt: Why was a movable cloth version useful before finishing the jacket?
options: It showed that the final jacket would never require further changes.
It allowed Jonas to avoid testing the jacket while sitting.
It made all three testers prefer the same pocket position.
It made experimentation cheaper and easier to revise.
questions.explanation: 可移动的布样让他无需每次裁剪昂贵材料即可比较位置，因此降低了试验成本，也方便修改方案。
questions.quote: This allowed Jonas to test several positions without cutting expensive material each time.

questions.prompt: What does "garment" mean in the last paragraph?
options: A tool used for cutting material.
A piece of clothing.
A person who tests a pocket.
A plan for a classroom presentation.
questions.explanation: 上下文一直讨论夹克及衣物如何随人体活动，garment 在此是指一件衣服，而非制作工具或展示计划。
questions.quote: A useful garment had to work with a moving person, whose daily actions were more complicated than the still pose of a display stand.

reading.title: 同一个地名的两种读法
reading.subtitle: Hearing the Names on the Map
reading.body:
When a college radio group prepared a programme about local place names, its members began with a printed map. They planned to read each name aloud and explain where it came from. The first interview complicated this simple idea. Two long-term residents pronounced the name of the same hill differently, and both had used their version since childhood.

The students initially asked which pronunciation was correct. One interviewee suggested a different question: who used each version, and in what situations? She used one form at home and another when giving directions to visitors. A second speaker associated his version with the village where he had grown up. The differences carried stories about family and movement that the map could not display.

The group decided to include several voices rather than appoint one speaker as the authority for the whole area. Each recording was introduced with a short description approved by the person speaking. Where an explanation of a name's origin was based on a family story rather than a written record, the programme said so. The students wanted to preserve the stories without presenting every memory as a confirmed historical fact.

After the broadcast, a listener sent a recording from her grandmother, who used another version of one name. The students added it to their project page with permission. Their programme had started as a guide to saying names correctly and become an invitation to listen more closely. A familiar label on a map could hold more than one pronunciation, and those differences could reveal connections that a single official spelling left unheard.

questions.prompt: What is the passage mainly about?
options: Why written maps should include only one local voice.
How students proved that all family stories were historically accurate.
Why visitors should avoid using unfamiliar place names.
How exploring varied pronunciations revealed local experiences and connections.
questions.explanation: 项目由寻找唯一正确读音转为记录多种地方声音，并从中认识家庭、迁移和使用情境所承载的联系。
questions.quote: The differences carried stories about family and movement that the map could not display.

questions.prompt: How did the programme treat explanations based on family stories?
options: It removed all of them before the broadcast.
It identified them as family stories rather than written evidence.
It presented them as official meanings printed on the map.
It asked one speaker to choose which stories were true.
questions.explanation: 节目明确区分家族口述和书面记录，既保留故事，也不把所有记忆都表述为已证实的历史事实。
questions.quote: Where an explanation of a name's origin was based on a family story rather than a written record, the programme said so.

questions.prompt: What does the interviewee's use of two pronunciations suggest?
options: She had forgotten the name printed on the map.
The two forms referred to entirely different hills.
A person's choice of pronunciation can depend on the audience.
One form had been forbidden during local broadcasts.
questions.explanation: 受访者在家中和给游客指路时使用不同读法，说明同一个人的语言选择也可能随着交流对象改变。
questions.quote: She used one form at home and another when giving directions to visitors.

questions.prompt: What does "authority" mean in the third paragraph?
options: Someone accepted as having the final or most reliable judgement.
A device used to record an interview.
An organisation responsible for printing maps.
A visitor asking for directions to a hill.
questions.explanation: 学生选择呈现多位说话者而非由一人定全地区的标准，因此 authority 在此指拥有最终判断地位的权威。
questions.quote: The group decided to include several voices rather than appoint one speaker as the authority for the whole area.

reading.title: 海滩上没有捡走的东西
reading.subtitle: A Survey Beyond the Most Striking Object
reading.body:
On a field trip to a fictional coastal village, a geography class surveyed objects washed onto a beach. The most striking discovery was a large wooden crate near the water. Several students photographed it immediately and suggested making it the centre of their report. Their teacher asked them to finish the planned survey before deciding what story the beach told.

The class had divided an accessible part of the shore into equal sections. In each section, students noted the kinds of objects visible within a marked area. They did not enter the water or handle unfamiliar items. The crate stood outside those marked areas, so it belonged in a separate observation note. Including it in the main count would change the method simply because an object was especially interesting.

After comparing their records, the students found many small pieces of rope and very few large wooden objects. They also noticed that two sections contained much more material than the others. Instead of assuming that the whole beach looked the same, they marked the differences on a sketch. A later visit might show a different pattern, so the report described the date and the area covered.

The final presentation opened with the photograph of the crate, but used it to introduce a question about attention. What catches the eye is not always what appears most often. The class still included unusual objects in a separate gallery. It simply kept those discoveries distinct from the systematic count. The beach offered both interesting stories and information that required a consistent way of looking.

vocabulary.meaning: 系统的；按既定方法进行的

questions.prompt: What is the main lesson of the beach survey?
options: Interesting discoveries should be distinguished from observations collected by a fixed method.
Large objects always provide the best account of a beach.
A report should exclude every photograph taken outside a marked area.
One visit can reveal a permanent pattern along an entire coast.
questions.explanation: 木箱可作为有趣发现展示，但不能随意加入既定区域的计数，文章强调显眼个例与系统记录的区别。
questions.quote: It simply kept those discoveries distinct from the systematic count.

questions.prompt: Why was the crate recorded separately from the main count?
options: It was the only object the students could identify.
It had already been removed before the class arrived.
It was outside the marked survey areas.
It was made of a material excluded from every observation.
questions.explanation: 调查依照标定区域进行，木箱在这些区域之外，所以被放入单独的观察备注而非主计数。
questions.quote: The crate stood outside those marked areas, so it belonged in a separate observation note.

questions.prompt: Why did the students mark differences between sections on a sketch?
options: They wanted the sketch to replace all the written records.
They recognised that one uniform description would hide local variation.
They had decided that only the cleanest section mattered.
They believed the crate had caused every difference along the shore.
questions.explanation: 两个区段的物品明显更多，绘图保留这些空间差异，有助于避免用一个统一描述掩盖海滩各处的不同情况。
questions.quote: Instead of assuming that the whole beach looked the same, they marked the differences on a sketch.

questions.prompt: What does "striking" mean in the first paragraph?
options: Dangerous to handle without tools.
Common in every marked area.
Moving rapidly towards the water.
Noticeable and likely to attract attention.
questions.explanation: 学生看到大木箱就立即拍照并想以它为中心写报告，说明 striking 指外观显眼、容易引起注意。
questions.quote: Several students photographed it immediately and suggested making it the centre of their report.

reading.title: 照片的用途变了以后
reading.subtitle: A Photograph with a New Audience
reading.body:
At a student storytelling workshop, Farah photographed participants sharing memories in a small circle. Everyone had agreed that pictures could appear in a private online album for the group. One photograph showed a participant laughing while holding a drawing from her childhood. Farah thought it captured the friendly atmosphere especially well.

A month later, the organisers asked to use that image on a poster advertising the next workshop. Farah was ready to send the file, but then remembered the original agreement. The poster would appear around town and on an open website. This was a different audience from the people who had attended the session. She contacted the person in the photograph and explained exactly where the image would appear.

The participant was comfortable with the private album but did not want the childhood drawing shown publicly. Farah offered to crop the image, yet the participant still preferred another photograph to be used. Farah accepted the answer and helped select an image of empty chairs and colourful materials before the workshop began. The new poster conveyed an invitation without identifying anyone who had shared a personal memory.

At the next workshop, the organisers described possible uses of photographs before taking them. Participants could choose whether to join a group picture intended for publicity, separately from appearing in the private album. Farah did not regard the earlier photograph as wasted work. It still served the purpose that everyone had accepted. The experience taught her to ask whether permission matched a particular use, rather than treating one agreement as permission for every future audience.

questions.prompt: What is the main message of the passage?
options: Photographs of people are unsuitable for every kind of poster.
Private albums should always be deleted after a workshop.
Agreement to one use of a photograph should not be assumed to cover another.
A photographer should decide which personal details are harmless to display.
questions.explanation: 私人相册与公开海报面对不同受众，法拉重新确认当事人意愿，说明许可应对应具体用途而非自动扩展。
questions.quote: The experience taught her to ask whether permission matched a particular use, rather than treating one agreement as permission for every future audience.

questions.prompt: What image was chosen for the new poster?
options: Empty chairs and colourful materials before the workshop.
The childhood drawing with the person's face removed.
A group picture taken at the end of the first workshop.
The original image with a different background colour.
questions.explanation: 当事人不愿照片公开后，法拉协助改选了活动开始前空椅子和彩色材料的照片来制作宣传海报。
questions.quote: Farah accepted the answer and helped select an image of empty chairs and colourful materials before the workshop began.

questions.prompt: Why did cropping the image not settle the matter?
options: The organisers had already printed the original poster.
Cropping would have made the file too large to send.
The private album no longer contained the photograph.
The participant's preference still applied to the proposed public use.
questions.explanation: 裁剪只是一种技术方案，并不能替代当事人的选择；她仍希望使用另一张照片，因此法拉继续尊重这一意愿。
questions.quote: Farah offered to crop the image, yet the participant still preferred another photograph to be used.

questions.prompt: What does "publicity" mean in the last paragraph?
options: Private discussion among the original participants.
Material or activity intended to attract public attention.
A record kept only for the photographer's practice.
An instruction for cropping a digital photograph.
questions.explanation: 文中把用于宣传的合影与私人相册分开选择，因此 publicity 指向公众推广活动、吸引关注的用途。
questions.quote: Participants could choose whether to join a group picture intended for publicity, separately from appearing in the private album.

reading.title: 领养介绍卡之外
reading.subtitle: Meeting the Cat Behind the Description
reading.body:
When Owen began volunteering at a small animal shelter, he helped write introduction cards for cats waiting for new homes. He wanted every card to sound cheerful. A quiet cat called Pebble became a friendly companion who enjoyed company. Owen had seen her sit beside an experienced volunteer, so the description seemed reasonable to him.

During an open afternoon, several visitors expected Pebble to approach them immediately. Instead, she stayed at the back of her space. Owen worried that the card had created the wrong expectation. The volunteer explained that Pebble usually took time to become comfortable with unfamiliar people. Sitting quietly nearby had been part of the relationship Owen observed, although it was missing from his short description.

Together, they rewrote the card to describe situations rather than attach a broad label. Pebble often sat beside a familiar person during quiet reading sessions, but usually watched new visitors from a distance at first. The shelter also arranged appointments where interested visitors could spend an unhurried period with a volunteer and ask about daily routines. No visitor was expected to make a decision during that first meeting.

Later, a visitor said that the more detailed card helped her understand what meeting Pebble might be like. Owen could not know whether this particular meeting would lead to adoption, and he did not promise a certain outcome. He had found a more useful role for his writing. Instead of making every animal sound immediately appealing to everyone, he could help people ask better questions about the kind of relationship they were ready to build.

questions.prompt: What does Owen learn about writing introduction cards?
options: Every animal should be described with the same cheerful label.
Only experienced volunteers should speak to visitors.
Visitors need a promise that an animal will behave in one fixed way.
Specific descriptions can help visitors form more realistic expectations.
questions.explanation: 宽泛的友好标签让访客期待立即亲近，加入熟悉程度和场景细节后，介绍卡能帮助形成更符合实际的认识。
questions.quote: Together, they rewrote the card to describe situations rather than attach a broad label.

questions.prompt: What did Pebble usually do when meeting new visitors?
options: She immediately sat beside them during reading sessions.
She watched them from a distance at first.
She followed them around the open afternoon.
She approached each person as soon as they arrived.
questions.explanation: 修改后的介绍明确写道，Pebble 对新访客通常先保持距离观察，熟悉的人身边才较常出现安静陪伴。
questions.quote: Pebble often sat beside a familiar person during quiet reading sessions, but usually watched new visitors from a distance at first.

questions.prompt: Why did Owen's first observation lead to an incomplete description?
options: He had watched a different cat without realising it.
The experienced volunteer had asked him to hide the cat's behaviour.
He had overlooked how familiarity influenced the interaction.
The shelter never allowed cats to meet unfamiliar visitors.
questions.explanation: 欧文看到了猫陪伴熟悉志愿者的结果，却没把逐步建立熟悉感的过程写进去，因此把特定情境概括得过广。
questions.quote: Sitting quietly nearby had been part of the relationship Owen observed, although it was missing from his short description.

questions.prompt: What does "unhurried" mean in the third paragraph?
options: Allowing enough time without pressure to rush.
Limited to a very short conversation.
Suitable only for experienced volunteers.
Certain to lead to an immediate decision.
questions.explanation: 后一句说明首次见面不要求决定是否领养，可见 unhurried 强调时间充足、没有匆忙作决定的压力。
questions.quote: No visitor was expected to make a decision during that first meeting.
